Corollary~\ref{cor:aff} (every source),
$(1-a)R_{\mathrm{Rt}}<p_{k+1}+(1-a)C$ (or $=0$ for a singleton, when the
same bound holds trivially).
nodes.statement_short: Leader isolated within the left part; expand $R$ and bound the right part by Corollary 2.

nodes.name: Two left symbols
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Two left symbols.} Then $L'=\{p_2\}$, so $x=p_2=p_k$ and $xR_{L'}=0$;
with $p_{k+1}\le p_k=x$,
\[
  R\ <\ (1+a)-\mathrm H(p_1,x,1-a)+x+(1-a)\,C\ =\ F(p_1,x),
\]
and $|2x-\delta|\le p_k=x$ reads $x\ge\tfrac\delta3$
\textup{(}$\delta-2x\le x$\textup{)} and $x\le\delta$
\textup{(}$2x-\delta\le x$\textup{)}.
nodes.statement_short: $R<F(p_1,x)$ with $x\in[\delta/3,\delta]$.

nodes.name: At least three left symbols
nodes.statement:
\textbf{At least three left symbols.} Then $|L'|\ge2$ and $xR_{L'}<p_2+xC$
(Corollary~\ref{cor:aff} again); since $p_2$ and $p_k$ are distinct symbols of
$L'$, $p_2+p_{k+1}\le p_2+p_k\le x$, whence $R<F(p_1,x)+xC=G(p_1,x)$.
Moreover $p_k\le\min(p_2,\,x-p_2)\le\tfrac x2$, so $|2x-\delta|\le\tfrac x2$:
$x\ge\tfrac{2\delta}5$ and $x\le\tfrac{2\delta}3$.
nodes.statement_short: $R<G(p_1,x)$ with $x\in[2\delta/5,2\delta/3]$.

nodes.name: Maximise at endpoints
nodes.statement:
For the endpoints, in $x$, with $t:=1-p_1-x$ and $\mathrm I'(t)=-\log_2 t-\log_2 e$,
\[
  \frac{\partial F}{\partial x}\ =\ 2-C+\log_2\frac{x}{t},
  \qquad
  \frac{\partial G}{\partial x}\ =\ 2+\log_2\frac{x}{t},
\]
both strictly increasing in $x$ ($x$ increases, $t$ decreases); so
$F(p_1,\cdot)$ and $G(p_1,\cdot)$ are decreasing-then-increasing and each is
maximised over its $x$-interval at an endpoint.
nodes.statement_short: $\partial_x F$, $\partial_x G$ increase, so maxima are at the interval endpoints.

nodes.name: Comparisons with B-tilde
nodes.statement:
Write $W_{\mathrm{iso}}(p_1):=\bigl(1-\mathrm H_2(p_1)\bigr)+(1-p_1)K$ and
$T_0(x):=3-3x-2\mathrm I(x)-\mathrm I(1-2x)$; by the grouping identity,
$T_0(x)=(1-\mathrm H_2(x))+(1-x)V\bigl(\tfrac{x}{1-x}\bigr)$. On
$[\tfrac13,\tfrac12]$, with $\delta=1-2p_1$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textup{(o)}] $\tfrac13+C<K$:
  $\ K-\tfrac13-C=\tfrac56\log_25-\tfrac{11}6>0$.
\item[\textup{(i)}] $W_{\mathrm{iso}}\le\tilde B$, by pure algebra: since
  $K=\tfrac{1+C}2$, the $\mathrm H_2$-terms cancel and
  \[
  \begin{aligned}
    \tilde B(p_1)-W_{\mathrm{iso}}(p_1)\ &=\ (1+C)\,p_1-(1-p_1)\,\frac{1+C}{2}\\
    &=\ \frac{(1+C)(3p_1-1)}{2}\ \ge\ 0 .
  \end{aligned}
  \]
\item[\textup{(ii)}] $T_0\le\tilde B$: the difference
  $\tilde B-T_0=-2+(4+C)\,p_1+\mathrm I(p_1)-\mathrm I(1-p_1)+\mathrm I(\delta)$ is
  concave, with endpoint values $\tfrac{C}3>0$ at $\tfrac13$ and
  $\tfrac{C}2>0$ at $\tfrac12$.
\item[\textup{(iii)}] $F(\cdot,\delta)\le\tilde B$: since $1-p_1-\delta=p_1$,
  $F(p_1,\delta)=T_0(p_1)+C\,p_1$, and
  \[
    \tilde B-F(\cdot,\delta)\ =\ -2+4p_1+\mathrm I(p_1)-\mathrm I(1-p_1)+\mathrm I(\delta)
  \]
  is concave and vanishes at both endpoints: $\tilde B$ is exactly the
  concave curve pinned to the worst two-left-symbol bound at $p_1=\tfrac13$ and
  at $p_1=\tfrac12$.
\item[\textup{(iv)}] $F(\cdot,\tfrac\delta3)\le\tilde B$: the difference is
  concave with endpoint values
  $-\tfrac49+\tfrac23\log_23-\tfrac5{27}\log_25>0$ at $\tfrac13$
  and $0$ at $\tfrac12$.
\item[\textup{(v)}] $G(\cdot,\tfrac{2\delta}5)\le\tilde B$: the difference is
  concave with endpoint values $-\tfrac83+\tfrac{11}9\log_25>0$
  at $\tfrac13$ and $0$ at $\tfrac12$.
\item[\textup{(vi)}] $G(\cdot,\tfrac{2\delta}3)\le\tilde B$: the difference is
  concave with endpoint values
  $-\tfrac{20}9+\tfrac23\log_23+\tfrac59\log_25>0$ at $\tfrac13$
  and $0$ at $\tfrac12$.
\end{enumerate}
In \textup{(ii)}--\textup{(vi)}, concavity places each difference above the
smaller endpoint value on all of $[\tfrac13,\tfrac12]$, hence $\ge0$ there.
nodes.statement_short: On $[1/3,1/2]$ every comparison curve ($W_{iso}$, $T_0$, $F$, $G$ endpoints) lies below $\tilde B$; also $1/3+C<K$.
nodes.label: lem:midcomp

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 11
nodes.statement:
In each of (ii)--(vi) the difference of the two curves is concave (a sum of
$\pm\mathrm I$ of affine arguments), so nonnegativity on $[\tfrac13,\tfrac12]$
follows from its two endpoint values; (o) and (i) are direct algebra.
\textbf{Concavity in
(ii)--(vi).} Each difference is affine plus terms $\pm \mathrm I(u(p_1))$ with $u$
affine of slope $s$, contributing $\pm s^2I''(u)=\mp\tfrac{s^2}{u\ln2}$ to
the second derivative; collecting them, the second derivatives times $\ln2$
are
\[
  \textup{(ii),(iii)}:\ -\tfrac1{p_1}-\tfrac4\delta+\tfrac1{1-p_1};\qquad
  \textup{(iv)}:\ -\tfrac4{3\delta}-\tfrac1{3(2-p_1)}+\tfrac1{1-p_1};
\]
\[
  \textup{(v)}:\ -\tfrac8{5\delta}-\tfrac1{5(3-p_1)}+\tfrac1{1-p_1};\qquad
  \textup{(vi)}:\ -\tfrac8{3\delta}-\tfrac1{3(1+p_1)}+\tfrac1{1-p_1},
\]
each negative: on $[\tfrac13,\tfrac12)$ one has $\tfrac1{1-p_1}\le2$, while
$\delta\le\tfrac13$ gives $\tfrac4\delta\ge12$, $\tfrac4{3\delta}\ge4$,
$\tfrac8{5\delta}\ge\tfrac{24}5$, $\tfrac8{3\delta}\ge8$, all $>2$.

\textbf{Endpoints at $\tfrac12$.} There $\delta=0$ and all four constrained
curves degenerate to
$F(\tfrac12,0)=G(\tfrac12,0)=\tfrac32+\tfrac{C}2-\mathrm H_2(\tfrac12)=K
=\tilde B(\tfrac12)$, while $T_0(\tfrac12)=\tfrac12=\tilde B(\tfrac12)
-\tfrac{C}2$: the values claimed.

\textbf{Endpoints at $\tfrac13$}, where $\delta=\tfrac13$ and
$\tilde B(\tfrac13)=\tfrac{10}3-\log_23-\tfrac59\log_25$ (substitute
$C=4-\tfrac53\log_25$). For (ii):
$T_0(\tfrac13)=2-3\mathrm I(\tfrac13)=2-\log_23$, so $\tilde
B(\tfrac13)-T_0(\tfrac13)=\tfrac{C}3$. For (iii): using
$\mathrm I(\tfrac13)=\tfrac{\log_23}3$ and $\mathrm I(\tfrac23)=\tfrac23(\log_23-1)$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &-2+\tfrac43+\mathrm I\bigl(\tfrac13\bigr)-\mathrm I\bigl(\tfrac23\bigr)
  +\mathrm I\bigl(\tfrac13\bigr)\\
  &\quad=\ -\tfrac23+\tfrac{\log_23}3-\tfrac23(\log_23-1)+\tfrac{\log_23}3\ =\ 0 .
\end{aligned}
\]
For (iv)--(vi), evaluating $\mathrm H$ at the argument triples
$\bigl(\tfrac13,\tfrac19,\tfrac59\bigr)$,
$\bigl(\tfrac13,\tfrac2{15},\tfrac8{15}\bigr)$,
$\bigl(\tfrac13,\tfrac29,\tfrac49\bigr)$ and subtracting from
$\tilde B(\tfrac13)$ yields the closed forms in (iv)--(vi), each positive.
nodes.statement_short: Each difference is concave (sum of $\pm\mathrm I$ of affine arguments), so nonnegativity follows from the endpoint values.

nodes.name: Reduction to endpoints
nodes.statement:
In each of (ii)--(vi) the difference of the two curves is concave (a sum of
$\pm\mathrm I$ of affine arguments), so nonnegativity on $[\tfrac13,\tfrac12]$
follows from its two endpoint values; (o) and (i) are direct algebra.
nodes.statement_short: Concave differences are determined by their endpoint signs.

nodes.name: Concavity
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Concavity in
(ii)--(vi).} Each difference is affine plus terms $\pm \mathrm I(u(p_1))$ with $u$
affine of slope $s$, contributing $\pm s^2I''(u)=\mp\tfrac{s^2}{u\ln2}$ to
the second derivative; collecting them, the second derivatives times $\ln2$
are
\[
  \textup{(ii),(iii)}:\ -\tfrac1{p_1}-\tfrac4\delta+\tfrac1{1-p_1};\qquad
  \textup{(iv)}:\ -\tfrac4{3\delta}-\tfrac1{3(2-p_1)}+\tfrac1{1-p_1};
\]
\[
  \textup{(v)}:\ -\tfrac8{5\delta}-\tfrac1{5(3-p_1)}+\tfrac1{1-p_1};\qquad
  \textup{(vi)}:\ -\tfrac8{3\delta}-\tfrac1{3(1+p_1)}+\tfrac1{1-p_1},
\]
each negative: on $[\tfrac13,\tfrac12)$ one has $\tfrac1{1-p_1}\le2$, while
$\delta\le\tfrac13$ gives $\tfrac4\delta\ge12$, $\tfrac4{3\delta}\ge4$,
$\tfrac8{5\delta}\ge\tfrac{24}5$, $\tfrac8{3\delta}\ge8$, all $>2$.
nodes.statement_short: Second derivatives are negative on $[1/3,1/2)$.

nodes.name: Endpoints at 1/2
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Endpoints at $\tfrac12$.} There $\delta=0$ and all four constrained
curves degenerate to
$F(\tfrac12,0)=G(\tfrac12,0)=\tfrac32+\tfrac{C}2-\mathrm H_2(\tfrac12)=K
=\tilde B(\tfrac12)$, while $T_0(\tfrac12)=\tfrac12=\tilde B(\tfrac12)
-\tfrac{C}2$: the values claimed.
nodes.statement_short: All constrained curves degenerate to $K$ at $1/2$.

nodes.name: Endpoints at 1/3
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Endpoints at $\tfrac13$}, where $\delta=\tfrac13$ and
$\tilde B(\tfrac13)=\tfrac{10}3-\log_23-\tfrac59\log_25$ (substitute
$C=4-\tfrac53\log_25$). For (ii):
$T_0(\tfrac13)=2-3\mathrm I(\tfrac13)=2-\log_23$, so $\tilde
B(\tfrac13)-T_0(\tfrac13)=\tfrac{C}3$. For (iii): using
$\mathrm I(\tfrac13)=\tfrac{\log_23}3$ and $\mathrm I(\tfrac23)=\tfrac23(\log_23-1)$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &-2+\tfrac43+\mathrm I\bigl(\tfrac13\bigr)-\mathrm I\bigl(\tfrac23\bigr)
  +\mathrm I\bigl(\tfrac13\bigr)\\
  &\quad=\ -\tfrac23+\tfrac{\log_23}3-\tfrac23(\log_23-1)+\tfrac{\log_23}3\ =\ 0 .
\end{aligned}
\]
For (iv)--(vi), evaluating $\mathrm H$ at the argument triples
$\bigl(\tfrac13,\tfrac19,\tfrac59\bigr)$,
$\bigl(\tfrac13,\tfrac2{15},\tfrac8{15}\bigr)$,
$\bigl(\tfrac13,\tfrac29,\tfrac49\bigr)$ and subtracting from
$\tilde B(\tfrac13)$ yields the closed forms in (iv)--(vi), each positive.
nodes.statement_short: Closed-form evaluation at $1/3$.

nodes.name: Explicit form of the increasing envelope branch
nodes.statement:
The two branches of the envelope are the isolate curve $W_{\mathrm{iso}}$ of
Lemma~\ref{lem:midcomp} and the two-left-symbol endpoint curve at
$x=\tfrac\delta3$, whose explicit form (substitute $x=\tfrac\delta3$,
$1-p_1-x=\tfrac{2-p_1}3$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:fine}) is
\[
  F\bigl(p_1,\tfrac\delta3\bigr)
  \ =\ \frac{5-p_1}{3}+\frac{2-p_1}{3}\,C
  -\mathrm H\Bigl(p_1,\frac{1-2p_1}{3},\frac{2-p_1}{3}\Bigr).
\]
nodes.statement_short: The envelope branches are $W_{iso}$ and $F(p_1,\delta/3)$, written explicitly as $F_\ell(p_1)$.

nodes.name: Crossing of the middle branches
nodes.statement:
On $[\tfrac13,\tfrac12]$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textup{(a)}] $W_{\mathrm{iso}}$ is strictly decreasing, with
  $W_{\mathrm{iso}}'=\log_2\tfrac{p_1}{1-p_1}-K\le-K$; and $F(\cdot,\tfrac\delta3)$
  is strictly increasing, with slope at least
  $\tfrac{9\log_23+2\log_25-15}{9}\ge\tfrac{77}{180}$.
\item[\textup{(b)}] $\bigl(W_{\mathrm{iso}}-F(\cdot,\tfrac\delta3)\bigr)(\tfrac13)
  =-\tfrac49+\tfrac23\log_23-\tfrac5{27}\log_25>0$ and
  $\bigl(W_{\mathrm{iso}}-F(\cdot,\tfrac\delta3)\bigr)(\tfrac12)=-\tfrac K2<0$;
  hence there is a unique $p^*$ with
  $W_{\mathrm{iso}}(p^*)=F\bigl(p^*,\tfrac{\delta(p^*)}3\bigr)$, and
  $F(\cdot,\tfrac\delta3)\le W_{\mathrm{iso}}$ on $[\tfrac13,p^*]$,
  $W_{\mathrm{iso}}\le F(\cdot,\tfrac\delta3)$ on $[p^*,\tfrac12]$. Numerically
  $p^*=0.415798\ldots$, with common value $0.350664\ldots$
\item[\textup{(c)}] $\tfrac25<p^*<\tfrac7{16}$:
\[
  \bigl(W_{\mathrm{iso}}-F(\cdot,\tfrac\delta3)\bigr)\bigl(\tfrac25\bigr)
  =-\tfrac{83}{30}+\tfrac65\log_23+\tfrac7{18}\log_25\ >\ 0,
\]
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\bigl(F(\cdot,\tfrac\delta3)-W_{\mathrm{iso}}\bigr)\bigl(\tfrac7{16}\bigr)\\
  &\quad=\tfrac{119}{96}-\tfrac{27}{16}\log_23+\tfrac{185}{288}\log_25\ >\ 0 .
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{enumerate}
conclusions: hence there is a unique $p^*$ with
nodes.statement_short: $W_{iso}$ decreases and $F(\cdot,\delta/3)$ increases on $[1/3,1/2]$, so they cross once at $p^*\in(2/5,7/16)$.
nodes.label: lem:cross

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 12
nodes.statement:
The single difference $W_{\mathrm{iso}}-F(\cdot,\tfrac\delta3)$ is strictly
decreasing by (a), so its unique sign change and its signs at the interior
points $\tfrac25,\tfrac7{16}$ follow from the closed-form values below.
(a) $p_1\le1-p_1$ gives the first claim. Differentiating
$F(p_1,\tfrac\delta3)$ in $p_1$ (the $\log_2 e$-terms cancel, since the argument
slopes $1,-\tfrac23,-\tfrac13$ sum to zero):
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \tfrac{d}{dp_1}F\bigl(p_1,\tfrac\delta3\bigr)
  \ &=\ -\tfrac{1+C}{3}+\log_23+\log_2 p_1\\
  &\quad-\tfrac23\log_2\delta-\tfrac13\log_2(2-p_1)\\
  \ &\ge\ -\tfrac{1+C}{3}+\log_23-\tfrac{\log_25}3 \\
  \ &=\ \tfrac{9\log_23+2\log_25-15}{9},
\end{aligned}
\]
using $\log_2 p_1\ge-\log_23$, $\log_2\delta\le-\log_23$, $\log_2(2-p_1)\le\log_25-\log_23$
and $C=4-\tfrac53\log_25$; and $9\log_23+2\log_25>15$.

(b) The value at $\tfrac13$ is the endpoint value of
Lemma~\ref{lem:midcomp}(iv), since $W_{\mathrm{iso}}(\tfrac13)
=\tilde B(\tfrac13)$ by item (i) there; at $\tfrac12$,
$W_{\mathrm{iso}}(\tfrac12)=\tfrac K2$ while $F(\tfrac12,0)=K$. The
difference is strictly decreasing by (a), whence the unique zero and the sign
pattern.

(c) At $\tfrac25$ ($\delta=\tfrac15$): $\mathrm H_2(\tfrac25)
=\log_25-\tfrac25-\tfrac35\log_23$ gives $W_{\mathrm{iso}}(\tfrac25)
=\tfrac{29}{10}+\tfrac35\log_23-\tfrac32\log_25$, and
$\mathrm I(\tfrac1{15})=\tfrac1{15}(\log_23+\log_25)$,
$\mathrm I(\tfrac8{15})=\tfrac8{15}(\log_23+\log_25-3)$ give
$F(\tfrac25,\tfrac1{15})=\tfrac{17}3-\tfrac35\log_23-\tfrac{17}9\log_25$. At $\tfrac7{16}$ ($\delta=\tfrac18$): the terms
$\mathrm I(\tfrac7{16})$ cancel in the difference, which needs only
$\mathrm I(\tfrac1{24})=\tfrac1{24}(3+\log_23)$,
$\mathrm I(\tfrac{25}{48})=\tfrac{25}{48}(4+\log_23-2\log_25)$ and
$\mathrm I(\tfrac9{16})=\tfrac9{16}(4-2\log_23)$.
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate both branches; the difference is strictly decreasing, so its sign pattern follows from closed-form values.

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement:
The single difference $W_{\mathrm{iso}}-F(\cdot,\tfrac\delta3)$ is strictly
decreasing by (a), so its unique sign change and its signs at the interior
points $\tfrac25,\tfrac7{16}$ follow from the closed-form values below.
nodes.statement_short: The difference is strictly decreasing by (a); signs follow from closed forms.

nodes.name: (a) monotonicity
nodes.statement:
(a) $p_1\le1-p_1$ gives the first claim. Differentiating
$F(p_1,\tfrac\delta3)$ in $p_1$ (the $\log_2 e$-terms cancel, since the argument
slopes $1,-\tfrac23,-\tfrac13$ sum to zero):
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \tfrac{d}{dp_1}F\bigl(p_1,\tfrac\delta3\bigr)
  \ &=\ -\tfrac{1+C}{3}+\log_23+\log_2 p_1\\
  &\quad-\tfrac23\log_2\delta-\tfrac13\log_2(2-p_1)\\
  \ &\ge\ -\tfrac{1+C}{3}+\log_23-\tfrac{\log_25}3 \\
  \ &=\ \tfrac{9\log_23+2\log_25-15}{9},
\end{aligned}
\]
using $\log_2 p_1\ge-\log_23$, $\log_2\delta\le-\log_23$, $\log_2(2-p_1)\le\log_25-\log_23$
and $C=4-\tfrac53\log_25$; and $9\log_23+2\log_25>15$.
nodes.statement_short: Derivative bounds for both branches.

nodes.name: (b) sign change
nodes.statement:
(b) The value at $\tfrac13$ is the endpoint value of
Lemma~\ref{lem:midcomp}(iv), since $W_{\mathrm{iso}}(\tfrac13)
=\tilde B(\tfrac13)$ by item (i) there; at $\tfrac12$,
$W_{\mathrm{iso}}(\tfrac12)=\tfrac K2$ while $F(\tfrac12,0)=K$. The
difference is strictly decreasing by (a), whence the unique zero and the sign
pattern.
nodes.statement_short: Endpoint values from Lemma 11 give a unique zero $p^*$.

nodes.name: (c) locate p^*
nodes.statement:
(c) At $\tfrac25$ ($\delta=\tfrac15$): $\mathrm H_2(\tfrac25)
=\log_25-\tfrac25-\tfrac35\log_23$ gives $W_{\mathrm{iso}}(\tfrac25)
=\tfrac{29}{10}+\tfrac35\log_23-\tfrac32\log_25$, and
$\mathrm I(\tfrac1{15})=\tfrac1{15}(\log_23+\log_25)$,
$\mathrm I(\tfrac8{15})=\tfrac8{15}(\log_23+\log_25-3)$ give
$F(\tfrac25,\tfrac1{15})=\tfrac{17}3-\tfrac35\log_23-\tfrac{17}9\log_25$. At $\tfrac7{16}$ ($\delta=\tfrac18$): the terms
$\mathrm I(\tfrac7{16})$ cancel in the difference, which needs only
$\mathrm I(\tfrac1{24})=\tfrac1{24}(3+\log_23)$,
$\mathrm I(\tfrac{25}{48})=\tfrac{25}{48}(4+\log_23-2\log_25)$ and
$\mathrm I(\tfrac9{16})=\tfrac9{16}(4-2\log_23)$.
nodes.statement_short: Closed forms at $2/5$ and $7/16$.

nodes.name: Per-piece domination
nodes.statement:
Write $h:=W_{\mathrm{iso}}-F(\cdot,\delta)$ and, for a comparison curve $X$,
$e_X:=F(\cdot,\tfrac\delta3)-X$. On $[\tfrac13,\tfrac12]$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textup{(i)}] $h$ is concave, $h(\tfrac13)=0$ exactly, and
\[
  h\bigl(\tfrac7{16}\bigr)
  =-\tfrac{37}{32}+\tfrac98\log_23+\tfrac{25}{96}\log_25-\tfrac7{16}\log_27\ >\ 0 .
\]
Hence $F(\cdot,\delta)\le W_{\mathrm{iso}}$
on $[\tfrac13,\tfrac7{16}]\supseteq[\tfrac13,p^*]$, and
$T_0=F(\cdot,\delta)-C\,p_1\le W_{\mathrm{iso}}$ there as well.
\item[\textup{(ii)}] $e_{F(\cdot,\delta)}$ is concave, vanishes at $\tfrac12$,
and $e_{F(\cdot,\delta)}(p^*)=h(p^*)\ge0$ by the crossing identity
$F(p^*,\tfrac{\delta}3)=W_{\mathrm{iso}}(p^*)$ and (i); hence
$F(\cdot,\delta)\le F(\cdot,\tfrac\delta3)$ on $[p^*,\tfrac12]$.
\item[\textup{(iii)}] $e_{G(\cdot,2\delta/5)}$, $e_{G(\cdot,2\delta/3)}$ and
$e_{T_0}$ are concave, with values $0$, $0$, $\tfrac{C}2$ at $\tfrac12$ and,
at $\tfrac25$,
\begin{multline*}
  e_{G(\cdot,2\delta/5)}\bigl(\tfrac25\bigr)
  =\tfrac{92}{75}-\tfrac35\log_23+\tfrac{32}{45}\log_25-\tfrac{13}{25}\log_213\\
  \ \ge\ -\tfrac{61}{75}-\tfrac{186}{175}\log_23+\tfrac{1696}{1575}\log_25
  \ >\ 0,
\end{multline*}
where the first lower bound is the chord bound
$\mathrm I(\tfrac{13}{25})\ge\tfrac57\,\mathrm I(\tfrac{64}{125})
+\tfrac27\,\mathrm I(\tfrac{27}{50})$ ($\mathrm I$ is concave and
$\tfrac{13}{25}=\tfrac57\cdot\tfrac{64}{125}+\tfrac27\cdot\tfrac{27}{50}$),
which eliminates $\log_213$, and the second is elementary; and
\begin{gather*}
  e_{G(\cdot,2\delta/3)}\bigl(\tfrac25\bigr)
  =\tfrac{16}{15}+\tfrac19\log_25-\tfrac7{15}\log_27>0,\\
  e_{T_0}\bigl(\tfrac25\bigr)
  =\tfrac{46}{15}-\tfrac35\log_23-\tfrac89\log_25>0 .
\end{gather*}
Hence $G(\cdot,\tfrac{2\delta}5)$,
$G(\cdot,\tfrac{2\delta}3)$, $T_0\le F(\cdot,\tfrac\delta3)$ on
$[\tfrac25,\tfrac12]\supseteq[p^*,\tfrac12]$.
\item[\textup{(iv)}] $W_{\mathrm{iso}}-G(\cdot,\tfrac{2\delta}5)$ and
$W_{\mathrm{iso}}-G(\cdot,\tfrac{2\delta}3)$ are concave, positive at
$\tfrac13$ (the endpoint values of
Lemma~\ref{lem:midcomp}(v),(vi), since
$W_{\mathrm{iso}}(\tfrac13)=\tilde B(\tfrac13)$), and positive at $\tfrac25$,
where each equals the certified sum
$\bigl(W_{\mathrm{iso}}-F(\cdot,\tfrac\delta3)\bigr)(\tfrac25)+e_G(\tfrac25)$
of Lemma~\ref{lem:cross}(c) and item (iii). Hence both $G$-curves are
$\le W_{\mathrm{iso}}$ on $[\tfrac13,\tfrac25]$; and on $[\tfrac25,p^*]$ as
well, via $G\le F(\cdot,\tfrac\delta3)\le W_{\mathrm{iso}}$ (item (iii) and
Lemma~\ref{lem:cross}(b),(c)).
\end{enumerate}
Consequently every curve considered ($W_{\mathrm{iso}}$, $T_0$,
$F(\cdot,\tfrac\delta3)$, $F(\cdot,\delta)$, $G(\cdot,\tfrac{2\delta}5)$,
$G(\cdot,\tfrac{2\delta}3)$) is $\le W_{\mathrm{iso}}$ on $[\tfrac13,p^*]$
and $\le F(\cdot,\tfrac\delta3)$ on $[p^*,\tfrac12)$.
conclusions:
Consequently every curve considered ($W_{\mathrm{iso}}$, $T_0$,
$F(\cdot,\tfrac\delta3)$, $F(\cdot,\delta)$, $G(\cdot,\tfrac{2\delta}5)$,
$G(\cdot,\tfrac{2\delta}3)$) is $\le W_{\mathrm{iso}}$ on $[\tfrac13,p^*]$
and $\le F(\cdot,\tfrac\delta3)$ on $[p^*,\tfrac12)$
nodes.statement_short: Every comparison curve is below $W_{iso}$ on $[1/3,p^*]$ and below $F(\cdot,\delta/3)$ on $[p^*,1/2)$.
nodes.label: lem:envdom

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 13
nodes.statement:
Every comparison below is between two curves whose difference is concave, so
its sign on the relevant subinterval is fixed by the closed-form values at the
endpoints $\tfrac13,\tfrac25,\tfrac7{16},\tfrac12$ computed here.
For concavity, as in Lemma~\ref{lem:midcomp}, each difference is affine
plus terms $\pm \mathrm I(u(p_1))$ with $u$ affine of slope $s$, contributing
$\mp\tfrac{s^2}{u\ln2}$ to the second derivative. Since $W_{\mathrm{iso}}$
and $\tilde B$ differ by an affine function
(Lemma~\ref{lem:midcomp}(i)), the differences in (i) and (iv) have the same
second derivatives as in Lemma~\ref{lem:midcomp}(iii),(v),(vi), and are
therefore concave. For
the differences against $F(\cdot,\tfrac\delta3)$, the second derivatives
times $\ln2$ are
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\text{(ii), }e_{T_0}:\ -\tfrac1{p_1}-\tfrac8{3\delta}+\tfrac1{3(2-p_1)};\\
  &e_{G(\cdot,2\delta/5)}:\
  -\tfrac4{15\delta}+\tfrac{9-2p_1}{15(2-p_1)(3-p_1)};\\
  &e_{G(\cdot,2\delta/3)}:\
  -\tfrac4{3\delta}-\tfrac{\delta}{3(2-p_1)(1+p_1)},
\end{aligned}
\]
all negative on $[\tfrac13,\tfrac12)$: $\tfrac1{3(2-p_1)}\le\tfrac29<
\tfrac8{3\delta}$, and $\tfrac{9-2p_1}{15(2-p_1)(3-p_1)}
\le\tfrac{25/3}{15\cdot\frac32\cdot\frac52}=\tfrac4{27}
<\tfrac45\le\tfrac4{15\delta}$ (as $\delta\le\tfrac13$).

\textbf{Exact values.} $h(\tfrac13)=0$: both $W_{\mathrm{iso}}$ and
$F(\cdot,\delta)$ equal $\tilde B$ at $\tfrac13$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:midcomp}(i),(iii)). At $\tfrac12$: $\delta=0$ and
$F(\tfrac12,0)=G(\tfrac12,0)=K$, $T_0(\tfrac12)=K-\tfrac{C}2$ (proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:midcomp}), giving the values in (ii),(iii). For
$h(\tfrac7{16})$: with $\mathrm I(\tfrac7{16})=\tfrac7{16}(4-\log_27)$,
$\mathrm I(\tfrac9{16})=\tfrac9{16}(4-2\log_23)$, $\mathrm I(\tfrac18)=\tfrac38$, one gets
$W_{\mathrm{iso}}(\tfrac7{16})=-\tfrac{51}{32}+\tfrac98\log_23
-\tfrac{15}{32}\log_25+\tfrac7{16}\log_27$ and
$F(\tfrac7{16},\tfrac18)=-\tfrac7{16}-\tfrac{35}{48}\log_25
+\tfrac78\log_27$.

At $\tfrac25$ ($\delta=\tfrac15$), with
$F(\tfrac25,\tfrac1{15})=\tfrac{17}3-\tfrac35\log_23-\tfrac{17}9\log_25$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:cross}):
\[
\begin{aligned}
  G\bigl(\tfrac25,\tfrac2{25}\bigr)
  &=\tfrac{111}{25}-\tfrac{13}5\log_25+\tfrac{13}{25}\log_213,\\
  G\bigl(\tfrac25,\tfrac2{15}\bigr)
  &=\tfrac{23}5-\tfrac35\log_23-2\log_25+\tfrac7{15}\log_27,
\end{aligned}
\]
\[
  T_0\bigl(\tfrac25\bigr)=\tfrac{13}5-\log_25,
\]
and subtracting each from $F(\tfrac25,\tfrac1{15})$ gives the three stated
closed forms. For the chord bound, substitute
$\mathrm I(\tfrac{13}{25})=\tfrac{13}{25}\cdot2\log_25-\tfrac{13}{25}\log_213$ and
then $\mathrm I(\tfrac{64}{125})=\tfrac{64}{125}(3\log_25-6)$,
$\mathrm I(\tfrac{27}{50})=\tfrac{27}{50}(1+2\log_25-3\log_23)$.
nodes.statement_short: Concave differences checked at endpoints $1/3,2/5,7/16,1/2$ via closed-form values; a chord bound eliminates $\log_2 13$.

nodes.name: Concavity of all differences
nodes.statement:
Every comparison below is between two curves whose difference is concave, so
its sign on the relevant subinterval is fixed by the closed-form values at the
endpoints $\tfrac13,\tfrac25,\tfrac7{16},\tfrac12$ computed here.
For concavity, as in Lemma~\ref{lem:midcomp}, each difference is affine
plus terms $\pm \mathrm I(u(p_1))$ with $u$ affine of slope $s$, contributing
$\mp\tfrac{s^2}{u\ln2}$ to the second derivative. Since $W_{\mathrm{iso}}$
and $\tilde B$ differ by an affine function
(Lemma~\ref{lem:midcomp}(i)), the differences in (i) and (iv) have the same
second derivatives as in Lemma~\ref{lem:midcomp}(iii),(v),(vi), and are
therefore concave. For
the differences against $F(\cdot,\tfrac\delta3)$, the second derivatives
times $\ln2$ are
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\text{(ii), }e_{T_0}:\ -\tfrac1{p_1}-\tfrac8{3\delta}+\tfrac1{3(2-p_1)};\\
  &e_{G(\cdot,2\delta/5)}:\
  -\tfrac4{15\delta}+\tfrac{9-2p_1}{15(2-p_1)(3-p_1)};\\
  &e_{G(\cdot,2\delta/3)}:\
  -\tfrac4{3\delta}-\tfrac{\delta}{3(2-p_1)(1+p_1)},
\end{aligned}
\]
all negative on $[\tfrac13,\tfrac12)$: $\tfrac1{3(2-p_1)}\le\tfrac29<
\tfrac8{3\delta}$, and $\tfrac{9-2p_1}{15(2-p_1)(3-p_1)}
\le\tfrac{25/3}{15\cdot\frac32\cdot\frac52}=\tfrac4{27}
<\tfrac45\le\tfrac4{15\delta}$ (as $\delta\le\tfrac13$).
nodes.statement_short: All differences are concave; second derivatives are negative.

nodes.name: Exact values
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Exact values.} $h(\tfrac13)=0$: both $W_{\mathrm{iso}}$ and
$F(\cdot,\delta)$ equal $\tilde B$ at $\tfrac13$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:midcomp}(i),(iii)). At $\tfrac12$: $\delta=0$ and
$F(\tfrac12,0)=G(\tfrac12,0)=K$, $T_0(\tfrac12)=K-\tfrac{C}2$ (proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:midcomp}), giving the values in (ii),(iii). For
$h(\tfrac7{16})$: with $\mathrm I(\tfrac7{16})=\tfrac7{16}(4-\log_27)$,
$\mathrm I(\tfrac9{16})=\tfrac9{16}(4-2\log_23)$, $\mathrm I(\tfrac18)=\tfrac38$, one gets
$W_{\mathrm{iso}}(\tfrac7{16})=-\tfrac{51}{32}+\tfrac98\log_23
-\tfrac{15}{32}\log_25+\tfrac7{16}\log_27$ and
$F(\tfrac7{16},\tfrac18)=-\tfrac7{16}-\tfrac{35}{48}\log_25
+\tfrac78\log_27$.

nodes.name: Values at 2/5
nodes.statement:
At $\tfrac25$ ($\delta=\tfrac15$), with
$F(\tfrac25,\tfrac1{15})=\tfrac{17}3-\tfrac35\log_23-\tfrac{17}9\log_25$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:cross}):
\[
\begin{aligned}
  G\bigl(\tfrac25,\tfrac2{25}\bigr)
  &=\tfrac{111}{25}-\tfrac{13}5\log_25+\tfrac{13}{25}\log_213,\\
  G\bigl(\tfrac25,\tfrac2{15}\bigr)
  &=\tfrac{23}5-\tfrac35\log_23-2\log_25+\tfrac7{15}\log_27,
\end{aligned}
\]
\[
  T_0\bigl(\tfrac25\bigr)=\tfrac{13}5-\log_25,
\]
and subtracting each from $F(\tfrac25,\tfrac1{15})$ gives the three stated
closed forms. For the chord bound, substitute
$\mathrm I(\tfrac{13}{25})=\tfrac{13}{25}\cdot2\log_25-\tfrac{13}{25}\log_213$ and
then $\mathrm I(\tfrac{64}{125})=\tfrac{64}{125}(3\log_25-6)$,
$\mathrm I(\tfrac{27}{50})=\tfrac{27}{50}(1+2\log_25-3\log_23)$.
nodes.statement_short: Closed forms at $2/5$ and the chord bound for $\mathrm I(13/25)$.

nodes.name: Middle envelope
nodes.statement:
For every source with $\tfrac13\le p_1<\tfrac12$,
\[
  R\ <\ \begin{cases}
  \,W_{\mathrm{iso}}(p_1)\ =\ 1-\mathrm H_2(p_1)+(1-p_1)\,\dfrac{1+C}2,\\
  \qquad \tfrac13\le p_1\le p^*,\\[8pt]
  \,F\bigl(p_1,\tfrac\delta3\bigr)\ =\ \dfrac{5-p_1}{3}
    +\dfrac{2-p_1}{3}\,C\\
  \qquad -\mathrm H\Bigl(p_1,\dfrac{1-2p_1}{3},\dfrac{2-p_1}{3}\Bigr),\\
  \qquad p^*\le p_1<\tfrac12.
  \end{cases}
\]
nodes.statement_short: For $p_1\in[1/3,1/2)$, $R<W_{iso}(p_1)$ up to $p^*$ and $R<F_\ell(p_1)$ after: a V-shaped envelope.
nodes.label: thm:mid

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3
nodes.statement:
Write $E(p_1)$ for the right-hand side (well defined: the two curves agree at
$p^*$). Strong induction on $n$; a source with $p_1<\tfrac12$ has $n\ge3$,
and a block with maximal fraction in $[\tfrac13,\tfrac12)$ has at least three
symbols, so the induction is well founded. A sub-block with maximal fraction
$q$ is bounded by: $q+C$ if $q<\tfrac13$ (Corollary~\ref{cor:aff});
$E(q)<K$ if $q\in[\tfrac13,\tfrac12)$ (induction hypothesis, then the
monotonicity of the pieces, Lemma~\ref{lem:cross}(a): on the left piece
$E(q)\le W_{\mathrm{iso}}(\tfrac13)=2-\log_23+\tfrac{C}3<K$, since
$K-W_{\mathrm{iso}}(\tfrac13)=\log_23-\tfrac56-\tfrac5{18}\log_25\ge\tfrac{11}{108}>0$
\textup{(}by $\log_23>\tfrac{19}{12}$, $\log_25<\tfrac73$\textup{)}, and on the right piece
$E(q)<F(\tfrac12,0)=K$); $V(q)$ if $q\ge\tfrac12$
(Corollary~\ref{cor:isob}). So, exactly as before, every sub-block with
maximal fraction $q<\tfrac12$ has redundancy $<K$.

\textbf{Isolate root} ($2p_1+p_2\ge1$): here $R=(1-\mathrm H_2(p_1))+(1-p_1)R(\rho)$
with leader fraction $q=p_2/(1-p_1)\le y:=p_1/(1-p_1)$, and
$y\in[\tfrac12,1)$. If $q<\tfrac13$, then $R(\rho)<\tfrac13+C<K$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:midcomp}(o); if $q\in[\tfrac13,\tfrac12)$, then $R(\rho)<K$.
In both cases $R<(1-\mathrm H_2(p_1))+(1-p_1)K=W_{\mathrm{iso}}(p_1)$. If $q\ge\tfrac12$, then
$R(\rho)<V(q)\le\max\bigl(V(\tfrac12),V(y)\bigr)=\max\bigl(\tfrac12,V(y)\bigr)$,
since $V$ is convex on $[\tfrac12,y]\ni q$. If the maximum is $\tfrac12$,
then $R<(1-\mathrm H_2(p_1))+\tfrac{1-p_1}2<W_{\mathrm{iso}}$ (as $\tfrac12<K$);
otherwise $R<(1-\mathrm H_2(p_1))+(1-p_1)V(y)=T_0(p_1)$ by the grouping identity of
Lemma~\ref{lem:midcomp}. So the isolate root yields $R<W_{\mathrm{iso}}(p_1)$
or $R<T_0(p_1)$.

\textbf{Group root} ($2p_1+p_2<1$): Lemma~\ref{lem:fine} bounds $R$ strictly by
one of the four endpoint curves $F(p_1,\tfrac\delta3)$, $F(p_1,\delta)$,
$G(p_1,\tfrac{2\delta}5)$, $G(p_1,\tfrac{2\delta}3)$.

In every case $R$ is strictly below one of the six curves of
Lemma~\ref{lem:envdom}, and that lemma bounds each of them by
$W_{\mathrm{iso}}(p_1)$ on $[\tfrac13,p^*]$ and by $F(p_1,\tfrac\delta3)$ on
$[p^*,\tfrac12)$, i.e.\ by $E(p_1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Strong induction on $n$; isolate roots give $W_{iso}$ or $T_0$, group roots give Lemma 10's curves, all dominated by Lemma 13.

nodes.name: Induction and sub-block bounds
nodes.statement:
Write $E(p_1)$ for the right-hand side (well defined: the two curves agree at
$p^*$). Strong induction on $n$; a source with $p_1<\tfrac12$ has $n\ge3$,
and a block with maximal fraction in $[\tfrac13,\tfrac12)$ has at least three
symbols, so the induction is well founded. A sub-block with maximal fraction
$q$ is bounded by: $q+C$ if $q<\tfrac13$ (Corollary~\ref{cor:aff});
$E(q)<K$ if $q\in[\tfrac13,\tfrac12)$ (induction hypothesis, then the
monotonicity of the pieces, Lemma~\ref{lem:cross}(a): on the left piece
$E(q)\le W_{\mathrm{iso}}(\tfrac13)=2-\log_23+\tfrac{C}3<K$, since
$K-W_{\mathrm{iso}}(\tfrac13)=\log_23-\tfrac56-\tfrac5{18}\log_25\ge\tfrac{11}{108}>0$
\textup{(}by $\log_23>\tfrac{19}{12}$, $\log_25<\tfrac73$\textup{)}, and on the right piece
$E(q)<F(\tfrac12,0)=K$); $V(q)$ if $q\ge\tfrac12$
(Corollary~\ref{cor:isob}). So, exactly as before, every sub-block with
maximal fraction $q<\tfrac12$ has redundancy $<K$.
nodes.statement_short: Strong induction; every sub-block with maximal fraction $<1/2$ has redundancy $<K$.

nodes.name: Isolate root
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Isolate root} ($2p_1+p_2\ge1$): here $R=(1-\mathrm H_2(p_1))+(1-p_1)R(\rho)$
with leader fraction $q=p_2/(1-p_1)\le y:=p_1/(1-p_1)$, and
$y\in[\tfrac12,1)$. If $q<\tfrac13$, then $R(\rho)<\tfrac13+C<K$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:midcomp}(o); if $q\in[\tfrac13,\tfrac12)$, then $R(\rho)<K$.
In both cases $R<(1-\mathrm H_2(p_1))+(1-p_1)K=W_{\mathrm{iso}}(p_1)$. If $q\ge\tfrac12$, then
$R(\rho)<V(q)\le\max\bigl(V(\tfrac12),V(y)\bigr)=\max\bigl(\tfrac12,V(y)\bigr)$,
since $V$ is convex on $[\tfrac12,y]\ni q$. If the maximum is $\tfrac12$,
then $R<(1-\mathrm H_2(p_1))+\tfrac{1-p_1}2<W_{\mathrm{iso}}$ (as $\tfrac12<K$);
otherwise $R<(1-\mathrm H_2(p_1))+(1-p_1)V(y)=T_0(p_1)$ by the grouping identity of
Lemma~\ref{lem:midcomp}. So the isolate root yields $R<W_{\mathrm{iso}}(p_1)$
or $R<T_0(p_1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Isolate root gives $R<W_{iso}$ or $R<T_0$.

nodes.name: Group root
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Group root} ($2p_1+p_2<1$): Lemma~\ref{lem:fine} bounds $R$ strictly by
one of the four endpoint curves $F(p_1,\tfrac\delta3)$, $F(p_1,\delta)$,
$G(p_1,\tfrac{2\delta}5)$, $G(p_1,\tfrac{2\delta}3)$.
nodes.statement_short: Group root: Lemma 10's four endpoint curves.

nodes.name: Domination
nodes.statement:
In every case $R$ is strictly below one of the six curves of
Lemma~\ref{lem:envdom}, and that lemma bounds each of them by
$W_{\mathrm{iso}}(p_1)$ on $[\tfrac13,p^*]$ and by $F(p_1,\tfrac\delta3)$ on
$[p^*,\tfrac12)$, i.e.\ by $E(p_1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 13 bounds all six curves by $E(p_1)$.

nodes.name: Single formula bound B-tilde
nodes.statement:
For every source with $\tfrac13\le p_1<\tfrac12$,
\[
  R\ <\ \tilde B(p_1)\ =\ 1+(1+C)\,p_1-\mathrm H_2(p_1);
\]
indeed the envelope of Theorem~\ref{thm:mid} lies below $\tilde B$ pointwise,
strictly except at $p_1=\tfrac13$ and (in the limit) $p_1=\tfrac12$.
nodes.label: cor:bt

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 3
nodes.statement:
$W_{\mathrm{iso}}\le\tilde B$ is Lemma~\ref{lem:midcomp}(i), with equality
only at $\tfrac13$; $F(\cdot,\tfrac\delta3)\le\tilde B$ is
Lemma~\ref{lem:midcomp}(iv), with equality only at $\tfrac12$ (the difference
is concave, positive at $\tfrac13$, zero at $\tfrac12$).
nodes.statement_short: Both envelope branches lie below $\tilde B$ by Lemma 11 (i) and (iv).

nodes.name: Flat cap R < K
nodes.statement:
For every source with $p_1<\tfrac12$,
$\ R<K=\tfrac52-\tfrac56\log_25=0.565059\ldots$
nodes.statement_short: For $p_1<1/2$, $R<K=\frac52-\frac56\log_2 5\approx0.5651$.
nodes.label: cor:kcap

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 4
nodes.statement:
For $p_1<\tfrac13$: $R<p_1+C<\tfrac13+C<K$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:midcomp}(o). For $p_1\in[\tfrac13,p^*]$:
$R<W_{\mathrm{iso}}(p_1)\le W_{\mathrm{iso}}(\tfrac13)
=2-\log_23+\tfrac{C}3<K$, by the monotonicity of
Lemma~\ref{lem:cross}(a) and the $\tfrac{11}{108}$-certificate in the proof
of Theorem~\ref{thm:mid}. For $p_1\in[p^*,\tfrac12)$:
$R<F(p_1,\tfrac\delta3)<F(\tfrac12,0)=K$, again by
Lemma~\ref{lem:cross}(a).
nodes.statement_short: Case split on $p_1$: affine bound below $1/3$, monotonicity of the two envelope pieces above.

nodes.name: p_1 < 1/3
nodes.statement:
For $p_1<\tfrac13$: $R<p_1+C<\tfrac13+C<K$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:midcomp}(o).
nodes.statement_short: Affine bound and $1/3+C<K$.

nodes.name: p_1 in [1/3,p^*]
nodes.statement:
For $p_1\in[\tfrac13,p^*]$:
$R<W_{\mathrm{iso}}(p_1)\le W_{\mathrm{iso}}(\tfrac13)
=2-\log_23+\tfrac{C}3<K$, by the monotonicity of
Lemma~\ref{lem:cross}(a) and the $\tfrac{11}{108}$-certificate in the proof
of Theorem~\ref{thm:mid}.
nodes.statement_short: $W_{iso}$ decreasing, $W_{iso}(1/3)<K$.

nodes.name: p_1 in [p^*,1/2)
nodes.statement:
For $p_1\in[p^*,\tfrac12)$:
$R<F(p_1,\tfrac\delta3)<F(\tfrac12,0)=K$, again by
Lemma~\ref{lem:cross}(a).
nodes.statement_short: $F(\cdot,\delta/3)$ increasing to $K$.

nodes.name: Domination of the affine bound on [1/3,1/2)
nodes.statement:
On $[\tfrac13,\tfrac12)$ the envelope of Theorem~\ref{thm:mid} is strictly
below $p_1+C$: the middle branches of Theorem~\ref{thm:main} improve the
affine bound wherever both apply. Quantitatively, the margin is at least
$\tfrac23C-c_3=1+\log_23-\tfrac{10}9\log_25=0.005042\ldots$ on the left
piece and at least $\tfrac{C}2=0.0650\ldots$ on the right piece.
conclusions:
the envelope of Theorem~\ref{thm:mid} is strictly
below $p_1+C$
nodes.statement_short: On $[1/3,1/2)$ the middle envelope is strictly below $p_1+C$, with margins $\frac23C-c_3$ and $C/2$.
nodes.label: prop:dom

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Left piece.} $p_1+C-W_{\mathrm{iso}}(p_1)$ has derivative
$1-W_{\mathrm{iso}}'=1+\log_2\tfrac{1-p_1}{p_1}+K>0$, so on $[\tfrac13,p^*]$ it
is minimised at $\tfrac13$, where (since
$W_{\mathrm{iso}}(\tfrac13)=\tilde B(\tfrac13)$) it equals
$\tfrac23C-c_3=-\beta$, the critical margin of Lemma~\ref{lem:caseA}
resurfacing.

\textbf{Right piece.} $p_1+C-F(p_1,\tfrac\delta3)$ is concave (its second
derivative times $\ln2$ is $-\tfrac1{p_1}-\tfrac4{3\delta}
-\tfrac1{3(2-p_1)}<0$), so on $[\tfrac25,\tfrac12]\supseteq[p^*,\tfrac12)$ it
is minimised at an endpoint. At $\tfrac12$ it equals $\tfrac{C}2$, and at
$\tfrac25$ it equals $-\tfrac{19}{15}+\tfrac35\log_23+\tfrac29\log_25$, which
exceeds $\tfrac{C}2$; so the margin is at least $\tfrac{C}2$ throughout.
nodes.statement_short: Monotone margin on the left piece, concave margin on the right piece, evaluated at endpoints.

nodes.name: Left piece
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Left piece.} $p_1+C-W_{\mathrm{iso}}(p_1)$ has derivative
$1-W_{\mathrm{iso}}'=1+\log_2\tfrac{1-p_1}{p_1}+K>0$, so on $[\tfrac13,p^*]$ it
is minimised at $\tfrac13$, where (since
$W_{\mathrm{iso}}(\tfrac13)=\tilde B(\tfrac13)$) it equals
$\tfrac23C-c_3=-\beta$, the critical margin of Lemma~\ref{lem:caseA}
resurfacing.
nodes.statement_short: Margin increasing; minimum $-\beta$ at $1/3$.

nodes.name: Right piece
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Right piece.} $p_1+C-F(p_1,\tfrac\delta3)$ is concave (its second
derivative times $\ln2$ is $-\tfrac1{p_1}-\tfrac4{3\delta}
-\tfrac1{3(2-p_1)}<0$), so on $[\tfrac25,\tfrac12]\supseteq[p^*,\tfrac12)$ it
is minimised at an endpoint. At $\tfrac12$ it equals $\tfrac{C}2$, and at
$\tfrac25$ it equals $-\tfrac{19}{15}+\tfrac35\log_23+\tfrac29\log_25$, which
exceeds $\tfrac{C}2$; so the margin is at least $\tfrac{C}2$ throughout.
nodes.statement_short: Concave margin, minimum $C/2$ at $1/2$.

nodes.name: Shape and quality of the middle envelope
nodes.statement:
The envelope decreases strictly from $2-\log_23+\tfrac{C}3=0.4584\ldots$ at
$\tfrac13$ to $0.350664\ldots$ at $p^*=0.415798\ldots$, then rises strictly
to $K=0.5651\ldots$ at $\tfrac12$, so the cap needs nothing beyond the
monotonicity of the two pieces; and by Proposition~\ref{prop:dom} no minimum
with the affine bound is ever active. Against the single curve of
Corollary~\ref{cor:bt} the envelope gains $(1+C)\tfrac{3p_1-1}2$ on the
left piece, up to $0.1398$ at $p^*$. Every improvement of the affine constant
$C$ halves into $K$.
nodes.statement_short: The envelope is V-shaped with minimum $0.3507$ at $p^*$; it gains up to $0.1398$ over $\tilde B$.
nodes.label: rem:midquality

nodes.name: Increasing envelope piece F_ell and envelope E
nodes.statement:
Throughout this section $\delta:=1-2p_1$,
$K=\tfrac{1+C}2$ and $V(q)=2-q-\mathrm H_2(q)$ are as in
Appendix~\ref{sec:midcap}, $W_{\mathrm{iso}}$ and $F(p_1,x)$ are the
envelope ingredients of Lemmas~\ref{lem:midcomp} and~\ref{lem:fine}
(the formula for $F$ makes sense for all $0<p_1<\tfrac12$, $0<x<1-p_1$,
and is so used below), and
\[
\begin{aligned}
  F_\ell(q)\ &:=\ F\bigl(q,\tfrac{1-2q}3\bigr)\\
  &\ =\ \frac{5-q}{3}+\frac{2-q}{3}\,C
  -\mathrm H\Bigl(q,\frac{1-2q}{3},\frac{2-q}{3}\Bigr)
\end{aligned}
\]
is the increasing piece of the envelope
$E=\max(W_{\mathrm{iso}},F_\ell)$.
nodes.statement_short: Reuse $\delta,K,V,W_{iso},F$; $F_\ell(q)=F(q,(1-2q)/3)$ and envelope $E=\max(W_{iso},F_\ell)$.

nodes.name: Charge bound for sub-blocks
nodes.statement:
Every sub-block is bounded using the results above: a block of absolute mass $m$
whose largest symbol is the fraction $q$ of $m$ contributes less than
$m\,\mathrm{ch}(q)$ to $R$ (and exactly $0$ if a singleton), where
\begin{equation} \mathrm{ch}(q)\;:=\;
  \begin{cases}
    q+C,\\
    \quad 0<q<\tfrac13
      \quad\text{(Corollary~\ref{cor:aff})},\\[2pt]
    E(q)=\max\bigl(W_{\mathrm{iso}}(q),\,F_\ell(q)\bigr),\\
    \quad \tfrac13\le q<\tfrac12
      \quad\text{(Theorem~\ref{thm:mid})},\\[2pt]
    V(q),\\
    \quad \tfrac12\le q<1
      \quad\text{(Corollary~\ref{cor:isob})}.
  \end{cases}
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: A block of mass $m$ with leader fraction $q$ contributes less than $m\,\mathrm{ch}(q)$, the piecewise bound from Cor. 2, Thm. 3, Cor. 1.

nodes.name: Charge function ch(q)
nodes.statement:
\mathrm{ch}(q)\;:=\;
  \begin{cases}
    q+C,\\
    \quad 0<q<\tfrac13
      \quad\text{(Corollary~\ref{cor:aff})},\\[2pt]
    E(q)=\max\bigl(W_{\mathrm{iso}}(q),\,F_\ell(q)\bigr),\\
    \quad \tfrac13\le q<\tfrac12
      \quad\text{(Theorem~\ref{thm:mid})},\\[2pt]
    V(q),\\
    \quad \tfrac12\le q<1
      \quad\text{(Corollary~\ref{cor:isob})}.
  \end{cases}
nodes.label: eq:charge-q

nodes.name: Exact values of the quarter-window curves
nodes.statement:
With $N_K(p_1):=1+2p_1-2\mathrm I(p_1)-\mathrm I(\delta)+\delta K$:
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\Pi\bigl(\tfrac14\bigr)=\tfrac14+\tfrac{C}2,\qquad
  N\bigl(\tfrac14\bigr)=\tfrac14,\\
  &\Theta\bigl(\tfrac14\bigr)=N_K\bigl(\tfrac14\bigr)=\tfrac{1+C}4,
\end{aligned}
\]
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \Pi\bigl(\tfrac13\bigr)&=F\bigl(\tfrac13,\tfrac16\bigr)=1+\tfrac{C-\log_23}2,\\
  \Theta\bigl(\tfrac13\bigr)&=F\bigl(\tfrac13,\tfrac19\bigr)
  =\tfrac{34}9-\tfrac53\log_23-\tfrac{10}{27}\log_25,
\end{aligned}
\]
\[
  F_\ell\bigl(\tfrac12\bigr)=F\bigl(\tfrac12,0\bigr)=K,\qquad
  \Theta-F\bigl(\cdot,\tfrac{1-\cdot}4\bigr)\ \text{is affine in }p_1 .
\]
nodes.statement_short: Closed-form values of $\Pi,\Theta,N,N_K,F$ at $1/4$, $1/3$ and $1/2$; $\Theta-F(\cdot,(1-\cdot)/4)$ is affine.
nodes.label: lem:exact-q

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 14
nodes.statement:
Every entropy term is of the form
$\mathrm I(a/b)=\tfrac ab\bigl(\log_2 b-\log_2 a\bigr)$, so each value is a
rational combination of logarithms of small integers. For example, at
$p_1=\tfrac13$,
$\Theta(\tfrac13)=\tfrac{4+2/3}{3}+\tfrac{4}{9}K-\mathrm H\bigl(\tfrac13,\tfrac29,\tfrac49\bigr)$
with
$\mathrm H\bigl(\tfrac13,\tfrac29,\tfrac49\bigr)
=\tfrac{\log_23}3+\tfrac29\bigl(\log_29-\log_22\bigr)+\tfrac49\bigl(\log_29-\log_24\bigr)
=\tfrac53\log_23-\tfrac{10}9$; substituting $K=\tfrac52-\tfrac56\log_25$ gives
$\Theta(\tfrac13)=\tfrac{34}9-\tfrac53\log_23-\tfrac{10}{27}\log_25$. The
remaining values are identical routine evaluations.
nodes.statement_short: Each entropy term at a rational point is a rational combination of logarithms; direct evaluation.

nodes.name: Rational log form
nodes.statement:
Every entropy term is of the form
$\mathrm I(a/b)=\tfrac ab\bigl(\log_2 b-\log_2 a\bigr)$, so each value is a
rational combination of logarithms of small integers.
nodes.statement_short: Entropy terms at rational points are rational combinations of logs.

nodes.name: Example Theta(1/3)
nodes.statement:
For example, at
$p_1=\tfrac13$,
$\Theta(\tfrac13)=\tfrac{4+2/3}{3}+\tfrac{4}{9}K-\mathrm H\bigl(\tfrac13,\tfrac29,\tfrac49\bigr)$
with
$\mathrm H\bigl(\tfrac13,\tfrac29,\tfrac49\bigr)
=\tfrac{\log_23}3+\tfrac29\bigl(\log_29-\log_22\bigr)+\tfrac49\bigl(\log_29-\log_24\bigr)
=\tfrac53\log_23-\tfrac{10}9$; substituting $K=\tfrac52-\tfrac56\log_25$ gives
$\Theta(\tfrac13)=\tfrac{34}9-\tfrac53\log_23-\tfrac{10}{27}\log_25$.
nodes.statement_short: Worked evaluation of $\Theta(1/3)$.

nodes.name: Remaining values
nodes.statement:
The
remaining values are identical routine evaluations.
nodes.statement_short: The other values are routine evaluations.

nodes.name: Certificates (signed evaluations)
nodes.statement:
Let $E_1,E_2,\Lambda_1,\Lambda_2,\Theta',\Theta''$ be the corner curves of
Propositions~\textup{\ref{prop:L2-q}}--\textup{\ref{prop:L3-q}} below.
The following exact signed evaluations hold on the endpoints used in the
corner reductions:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textup{(A1)}] $(\Pi-\Theta)(\tfrac13)
  =-\tfrac79+\tfrac76\log_23-\tfrac{25}{54}\log_25<0$.
\item[\textup{(A2)}] $(\Theta-N)(\tfrac13)
  =\tfrac{16}9-\tfrac23\log_23-\tfrac{10}{27}\log_25<0$.
\item[\textup{(A3)}] $(2-\log_23)-\Pi(\tfrac14)
  =\tfrac56\log_25-\log_23-\tfrac14>0$, and
  $\tfrac13+C-(2-\log_23)=\tfrac73+\log_23-\tfrac53\log_25>0$.
\item[\textup{(B1)}] $\tfrac13+C-F_\ell(\tfrac13)
  =\tfrac59+\tfrac53\log_23-\tfrac{35}{27}\log_25>0$.
\item[\textup{(C1)}] $\bigl(\Theta-F(\cdot,\tfrac\delta3)\bigr)(\tfrac14)
  =-\tfrac56+\tfrac34\log_23+\tfrac59\log_25-\tfrac7{12}\log_27>0$.
\item[\textup{(C2)}] $\bigl(\Theta-F(\cdot,\tfrac{1-\cdot}4)\bigr)(\tfrac14)
  =\tfrac78-\tfrac{21}{16}\log_23+\tfrac{25}{48}\log_25>0$;\quad
  $\bigl(\Theta-F(\cdot,\tfrac{1-\cdot}4)\bigr)(\tfrac13)
  =\tfrac79-\tfrac76\log_23+\tfrac{25}{54}\log_25>0$.
\item[\textup{(C3)}] $(\Theta-N_K)(\tfrac13)
  =\tfrac{23}{18}-\tfrac23\log_23-\tfrac5{54}\log_25>0$.
\item[\textup{(D1)}] $\Pi(\tfrac13)-E_1(\tfrac14)
  =\tfrac{17}{20}-\tfrac12\log_23+\tfrac56\log_25-\tfrac{11}{20}\log_2{11}>0$;\quad
  $\Pi(\tfrac13)-E_1(\tfrac13)
  =-\tfrac{12}5+\tfrac12\log_23+\tfrac{13}{18}\log_25>0$.
\item[\textup{(D2)}] $\Pi(\tfrac13)-E_2(\tfrac14)
  =\tfrac{11}{12}+\tfrac14\log_23-\tfrac59\log_25>0$;\quad
  $\Pi(\tfrac13)-E_2(\tfrac13)
  =-\tfrac{14}9+\tfrac76\log_23-\tfrac5{54}\log_25>0$.
\item[\textup{(D3)}] $\Pi(\tfrac13)-\Lambda_1(\tfrac14)
  =\tfrac5{28}-\tfrac54\log_23-\tfrac5{42}\log_25+\tfrac34\log_27>0$;\quad
  $\Pi(\tfrac13)-\Lambda_1(\tfrac13)
  =-\tfrac{26}{21}+\tfrac5{14}\log_23+\tfrac5{18}\log_25+\tfrac23\log_27
  -\tfrac{11}{21}\log_2{11}>0$.
\item[\textup{(D4)}] $\Pi(\tfrac13)-\Theta''(\tfrac14)
  =\tfrac5{36}+\log_23+\tfrac{25}{108}\log_25-\tfrac{19}{36}\log_2{19}>0$;\quad
  $\Pi(\tfrac13)-\Theta''(\tfrac13)
  =-\tfrac{16}9+\tfrac{11}6\log_23+\tfrac{25}{162}\log_25-\tfrac{14}{27}\log_27>0$.
\item[\textup{(D5)}] $(\Pi-\Lambda_2)(\tfrac14)
  =-\tfrac45-\tfrac65\log_23+\tfrac76\log_25>0$;\quad
  $(\Pi-\Lambda_2)(\tfrac13)
  =-\tfrac43+\tfrac3{10}\log_23+\tfrac{17}{18}\log_25-\tfrac7{15}\log_27>0$.
\item[\textup{(D6)}] $(\Pi-\Theta')(\tfrac14)
  =-\tfrac{11}{14}+\tfrac5{28}\log_25+\tfrac34\log_27-\tfrac{13}{28}\log_2{13}>0$;\quad
  $(\Pi-\Theta')(\tfrac13)
  =-\tfrac{38}{21}+\tfrac12\log_23-\tfrac5{14}\log_25+\tfrac23\log_27>0$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 15
nodes.statement:
As in Lemma~\ref{lem:exact-q}, each item is the evaluation of the stated
curves at a rational point, hence a rational combination of
$\log_23,\log_25,\log_27,\log_2{11},\log_2{13},\log_2{19},\log_2{23}$; the displayed
closed forms follow by collecting coefficients. For example, \textup{(A1)}
is $(\Pi-\Theta)(\tfrac13)$ with both values taken from
Lemma~\ref{lem:exact-q}:
$1+\tfrac{C-\log_23}2-\tfrac{34}9+\tfrac53\log_23+\tfrac{10}{27}\log_25
=-\tfrac79+\tfrac76\log_23-\tfrac{25}{54}\log_25$. Each sign then follows from
Lemma~\ref{lem:certify}\textup{(i)}: replacing each $\log_2 m$ by a rational
bound from its continued-fraction expansion reduces the sign to a comparison of
integer powers. Coarse bounds such as $\tfrac{19}{12}<\log_23<\tfrac{27}{17}$
suffice for the items with a comfortable margin; the near-degenerate ones,
\textup{(A1)}, \textup{(A2)}, \textup{(C2)}, and \textup{(S)}, use
correspondingly higher convergents \textup{(}for instance
$\log_23<\tfrac{485}{306}$, i.e.\ $3^{306}<2^{485}$\textup{)}.
nodes.statement_short: Evaluate at rational points and decide each sign by rational bounds on logarithms (Lemma 20(i)).

nodes.name: Right-part bound
nodes.statement:
Let $Q\in(0,1)$. Then $\sup_{0<q\le Q}\mathrm{ch}(q)\le M(Q)$, where
\[
  M(Q)\ :=\
  \begin{cases}
    Q+C, & Q<\tfrac13,\\[2pt]
    \max\bigl(\tfrac13+C,\;F_\ell(Q)\bigr), & \tfrac13\le Q<\tfrac12,\\[2pt]
    \max\bigl(K,\;V(Q)\bigr), & \tfrac12\le Q<1 ,
  \end{cases}
\]
and $M(Q)\le Q+C$ for all $Q<\tfrac12$.
nodes.statement_short: The charge $\mathrm{ch}(q)$ over $q\le Q$ is at most an explicit $M(Q)$, which is $\le Q+C$ for $Q<1/2$.
nodes.label: lem:msup-q

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 16
nodes.statement:
On $(0,\tfrac13)$ the bound $q+C$ increases to the limit
$\tfrac13+C$. On $[\tfrac13,\tfrac12)$, $E=\max(W_{\mathrm{iso}},F_\ell)$
with $W_{\mathrm{iso}}$ decreasing and $F_\ell$ increasing
(Lemma~\ref{lem:cross}(a)), so
$E(q)\le\max\bigl(W_{\mathrm{iso}}(\tfrac13),F_\ell(Q)\bigr)$ for
$q\le Q$; and $W_{\mathrm{iso}}(\tfrac13)\le\tfrac13+C$ is
$\tfrac32c_3\le C$. On $[\tfrac12,1)$,
$V$ is convex, so
$V(q)\le\max\bigl(V(\tfrac12),V(Q)\bigr)=\max\bigl(\tfrac12,V(Q)\bigr)$,
while the $[\tfrac13,\tfrac12)$ part contributes at most
$\max(\tfrac13+C,K)=K$ \textup{(}Lemma~\ref{lem:midcomp}(o)\textup{)},
and $\tfrac12<K$. For the last claim it remains to check
$F_\ell(Q)\le Q+C$ on $[\tfrac13,\tfrac12)$: the difference
$Q+C-F_\ell(Q)$ is concave \textup{(}$F_\ell$ is affine plus $-\mathrm I$ of
affine arguments, hence convex\textup{)}, so it is bounded below by the
smaller of its endpoint values $\tfrac13+C-F_\ell(\tfrac13)>0$
\textup{(}certificate \textup{(B1)}\textup{)} and
$\tfrac12+C-K=\tfrac{C}2>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Regime by regime: monotonicity of the envelope pieces and convexity of $V$; certificate (B1) for the last claim.

nodes.name: q < 1/3
nodes.statement:

nodes.statement_short: Affine charge increases to $1/3+C$.

$\tfrac32c_3\le C$.
nodes.statement_short: Monotone envelope pieces bound $E(q)$.

nodes.name: q in [1/2,1)
nodes.statement:

$V$ is convex, so
$V(q)\le\max\bigl(V(\tfrac12),V(Q)\bigr)=\max\bigl(\tfrac12,V(Q)\bigr)$,
while the $[\tfrac13,\tfrac12)$ part contributes at most
$\max(\tfrac13+C,K)=K$ \textup{(}Lemma~\ref{lem:midcomp}(o)\textup{)},
and $\tfrac12<K$.
nodes.statement_short: Convexity of $V$ and $1/2<K$.

nodes.name: M(Q) <= Q + C
nodes.statement:
For the last claim it remains to check
$F_\ell(Q)\le Q+C$ on $[\tfrac13,\tfrac12)$: the difference
$Q+C-F_\ell(Q)$ is concave \textup{(}$F_\ell$ is affine plus $-\mathrm I$ of

nodes.statement_short: Concave difference positive at both endpoints, by (B1).

nodes.name: No burial on [1/4,1/3)
conclusions: the root is a group split
the left part splits its leader off by itself: $2p_1+p_2\ge a$
the right part has at least two symbols
nodes.statement_short: For $p_1\in[1/4,1/3)$ the root is a group split, the leader sits at depth exactly 2, and $R$ obeys the two-level identity (11).
nodes.label: lem:noburial-q

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 17
nodes.statement:
(i) $2p_1+p_2\le3p_1<1$, so the root does not isolate the leader
(Lemma~\ref{lem:iso}); thus $k\ge2$, and the leader lies in $L$ since
blocks are prefixes.

(ii) Suppose $2p_1+p_2<a$, i.e.\ $p_2<a-2p_1$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:key},
$s\le p_k\le p_2<a-2p_1$. If $a\le\tfrac12$ then $1-2a<a-2p_1$ gives
$a>\tfrac{1+2p_1}3\ge\tfrac12$ (using $p_1\ge\tfrac14$), a contradiction;
if $a>\tfrac12$ then $2a-1<a-2p_1$ gives $a<1-2p_1\le\tfrac12$, again a
contradiction. Hence $2p_1+p_2\ge a$ and, by Lemma~\ref{lem:iso} applied
inside $L$, $L$ splits as $\{p_1\}\,|\,L'$: the leader is a leaf at depth
$2$. Identity \eqref{eq:master-q} is the recursion (Lemma~\ref{lem:rec})
at the root, the isolate reduction inside $L$, and the grouping identity
$(1-\mathrm H_2(a))+a\bigl(1-\mathrm H_2(p_1/a)\bigr)=(1+a)-\mathrm H(p_1,x,1-a)$, exactly
as in Lemma~\ref{lem:fine}.

(iii) If $B=\{p_n\}$ then $1-a=p_n\le p_k\le p_1$, so $a\ge1-p_1>\tfrac12$;
the bound $s\le p_k$ forces $p_k\ge2a-1\ge1-2p_1$, and $p_k\le p_1$ then
gives $p_1\ge\tfrac13$, a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: Isolation criterion and the key lemma; (ii) and (iii) by contradiction on the left mass $a$.

nodes.name: (i) group split
nodes.statement:
(i) $2p_1+p_2\le3p_1<1$, so the root does not isolate the leader
(Lemma~\ref{lem:iso}); thus $k\ge2$, and the leader lies in $L$ since
blocks are prefixes.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 5: the root does not isolate the leader.

nodes.name: (ii) leader at depth two
nodes.statement:
(ii) Suppose $2p_1+p_2<a$, i.e.\ $p_2<a-2p_1$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:key},
$s\le p_k\le p_2<a-2p_1$. If $a\le\tfrac12$ then $1-2a<a-2p_1$ gives
$a>\tfrac{1+2p_1}3\ge\tfrac12$ (using $p_1\ge\tfrac14$), a contradiction;
if $a>\tfrac12$ then $2a-1<a-2p_1$ gives $a<1-2p_1\le\tfrac12$, again a
contradiction. Hence $2p_1+p_2\ge a$ and, by Lemma~\ref{lem:iso} applied
inside $L$, $L$ splits as $\{p_1\}\,|\,L'$: the leader is a leaf at depth
$2$. Identity \eqref{eq:master-q} is the recursion (Lemma~\ref{lem:rec})
at the root, the isolate reduction inside $L$, and the grouping identity
$(1-\mathrm H_2(a))+a\bigl(1-\mathrm H_2(p_1/a)\bigr)=(1+a)-\mathrm H(p_1,x,1-a)$, exactly
as in Lemma~\ref{lem:fine}.
nodes.statement_short: Assuming $2p_1+p_2<a$ contradicts the key lemma; then isolate within $L$.

nodes.name: (iii) right part not a singleton
nodes.statement_short: A singleton right part forces $p_1\ge1/3$.

nodes.name: Two-level toll J, ratio Q and corner curves
nodes.statement:
Write
$J(a):=(1+a)-\mathrm H(p_1,\,a-p_1,\,1-a)\ge0$ for the two-level toll in
\eqref{eq:master-q} and $Q(a):=x/(1-a)$, strictly increasing in $a$, with
$J'(a)=1+\log_2 Q(a)$; the corner curves are ($N_K$ as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:exact-q}; in $\Lambda_1,\Lambda_2,\Theta',\Theta''$ the
toll $J$ is evaluated at the indicated left mass, with $x=a-p_1$ equal to
$\tfrac{3\delta}7,\tfrac{3\delta}5,\tfrac{4\delta}7,\tfrac{4\delta}9$
respectively):
\begin{align*}
  E_1(p_1)&:=2-p_1+\tfrac{3-p_1}{5}\,C-\mathrm I(p_1)\\
   &\phantom{{}:={}}-\mathrm I\Bigl(\tfrac{3-p_1}{5}\Bigr)-2\mathrm I\Bigl(\tfrac{1-2p_1}{5}\Bigr),\\
  E_2(p_1)&:=\tfrac{5-p_1}{3}+\tfrac{2-4p_1}{3}+\tfrac{1-2p_1}{3}
   +\tfrac{1+p_1}{3}\,C\\
   &\phantom{{}:={}}-\mathrm I(p_1)-\mathrm I\Bigl(\tfrac{1+p_1}{3}\Bigr)-2\mathrm I\Bigl(\tfrac{1-2p_1}{3}\Bigr),\\
  \Lambda_1(p_1)&:=J\Bigl(\tfrac{3+p_1}{7}\Bigr)+\tfrac{2\delta}{7}+(1-p_1)\,C,\\
  \Lambda_2(p_1)&:=J\Bigl(\tfrac{3-p_1}{5}\Bigr)+\tfrac{2\delta}{5}+(1-p_1)\,C,\\
  \Theta'(p_1)&:=J\Bigl(\tfrac{4-p_1}{7}\Bigr)+\tfrac{4\delta}{7}\,K\\
   &\phantom{{}:={}}+\tfrac{\delta}{7}+\tfrac{3+p_1}{7}\,C,\\
  \Theta''(p_1)&:=J\Bigl(\tfrac{4+p_1}{9}\Bigr)+\tfrac{4\delta}{9}\,K\\
   &\phantom{{}:={}}+\tfrac{\delta}{9}+\tfrac{5-p_1}{9}\,C .
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Toll $J(a)$, ratio $Q(a)=x/(1-a)$, and six corner curves $E_1,E_2,\Lambda_1,\Lambda_2,\Theta',\Theta''$.

nodes.name: Case |L'| = 1
assumptions: the left part has exactly two symbols
nodes.statement_short: With two left symbols, $R<\max\{F(p_1,\delta/3),F(p_1,(1-p_1)/4),\Theta,N_K,N\}$.
nodes.label: prop:L1-q

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3
nodes.statement:
Here $x=p_2=p_k\le p_1$ and $R_{L'}=0$, so by \eqref{eq:master-q} and
Lemma~\ref{lem:msup-q}, $R<h(a):=J(a)+(1-a)\,M(Q(a))$. The constraint
$s\le x$ reads $a\in[\tfrac{1+p_1}3,\,1-p_1]$, and $x\le p_1$ caps
$a\le2p_1$; since $p_1\ge\tfrac14>\tfrac15$ the window is
$[\tfrac{1+p_1}3,\,2p_1]$. Along it $Q$ increases from
$\delta/(2-p_1)<\tfrac13$ \textup{(}as $p_1>\tfrac15$\textup{)} through
$Q=\tfrac13$ at $a_{13}:=\tfrac{1+3p_1}4$ and $Q=\tfrac12$ at
$a_{12}:=\tfrac{1+2p_1}3$, to $Q(2p_1)=p_1/\delta\ge\tfrac12$
\textup{(}as $p_1\ge\tfrac14$; also $a_{13}\le a_{12}\le 2p_1$
there\textup{)}.

\textbf{On $[\tfrac{1+p_1}3,a_{13}]$} ($Q\le\tfrac13$):
$h(a)=J(a)+x+(1-a)C=F(p_1,x)$ with $x\in[\tfrac\delta3,\tfrac{1-p_1}4]$.
Since $\partial_xF=2-C+\log_2\tfrac{x}{1-p_1-x}$ is strictly increasing in
$x$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:fine}), $F$ is decreasing-then-increasing, so
$h\le\max\bigl(F(p_1,\tfrac\delta3),F(p_1,\tfrac{1-p_1}4)\bigr)$.

\textbf{On $[a_{13},a_{12}]$} ($\tfrac13\le Q\le\tfrac12$):
$h\le\max\bigl(\mathrm{fl}(a),\mathrm{co}(a)\bigr)$ pointwise, where
$\mathrm{fl}(a):=J(a)+(1-a)(\tfrac13+C)$ and
$\mathrm{co}(a):=J(a)+(1-a)F_\ell(Q(a))$. Since
$J'=1+\log_2 Q\le1+\log_2\tfrac12=0$ here, $\mathrm{fl}$ is decreasing, and
$\mathrm{fl}(a_{13})=F(p_1,\tfrac{1-p_1}4)$ \textup{(}at $Q=\tfrac13$
the two bounds agree\textup{)}. Expanding $(1-a)F_\ell(Q)$ by the scaled
grouping identity $(1-a)\sum_i \mathrm I(u_i)=\sum_i \mathrm I\bigl(u_i(1-a)\bigr)
-\mathrm I(1-a)$ \textup{(}$\sum_i u_i=1$\textup{)},
\[
  \begin{aligned}
  \mathrm{co}(a)=&(1+a)+\frac{5(1-a)-x}{3}
  +\frac{2(1-a)-x}{3}\,C\\
  &-\mathrm I(p_1)-2\mathrm I(x)\\
  &-\mathrm I\Bigl(\frac{1+2p_1-3a}{3}\Bigr)
  -\mathrm I\Bigl(\frac{2+p_1-3a}{3}\Bigr),
  \end{aligned}
\]
an affine function of $a$ plus terms $-\mathrm I(\text{affine})$, which is
convex. Hence
$\mathrm{co}\le\max\bigl(\mathrm{co}(a_{13}),\mathrm{co}(a_{12})\bigr)$;
$\mathrm{co}(a_{13})\le\mathrm{fl}(a_{13})$ because
$F_\ell(\tfrac13)\le\tfrac13+C$ \textup{(}certificate
\textup{(B1)}\textup{)}, and
$\mathrm{co}(a_{12})=J(a_{12})+(1-a_{12})K=\Theta(p_1)$ by
$F_\ell(\tfrac12)=K$ \textup{(}Lemma~\ref{lem:exact-q}\textup{)}.

\textbf{On $[a_{12},2p_1]$} ($Q\ge\tfrac12$):
$h\le\max\bigl(\mathrm{fl}_K(a),f(a)\bigr)$ pointwise, where
$\mathrm{fl}_K:=J+(1-a)K$ and $f:=J+(1-a)V(Q)$. $\mathrm{fl}_K$ is convex
($J''>0$), so
$\mathrm{fl}_K\le\max\bigl(\mathrm{fl}_K(a_{12}),\mathrm{fl}_K(2p_1)\bigr)
=\max\bigl(\Theta(p_1),N_K(p_1)\bigr)$. Expanding
$(1-a)\mathrm H_2(Q)=\mathrm I(x)+\mathrm I(1+p_1-2a)-\mathrm I(1-a)$,
\[
  f(a)=3-2a+p_1-\mathrm I(p_1)-2\mathrm I(a-p_1)-\mathrm I(1+p_1-2a),
\]
again convex, so $f\le\max\bigl(f(a_{12}),f(2p_1)\bigr)$; here
$f(a_{12})=J(a_{12})+(1-a_{12})V(\tfrac12)\le\Theta(p_1)$ \textup{(}as
$V(\tfrac12)=\tfrac12<K$\textup{)} and $f(2p_1)=N(p_1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $R$ by $h(a)=J(a)+(1-a)M(Q(a))$ on a window in $a$; split by the regime of $Q$ and use convexity on each piece.

nodes.name: Window in a
nodes.statement:
Here $x=p_2=p_k\le p_1$ and $R_{L'}=0$, so by \eqref{eq:master-q} and
Lemma~\ref{lem:msup-q}, $R<h(a):=J(a)+(1-a)\,M(Q(a))$. The constraint
$s\le x$ reads $a\in[\tfrac{1+p_1}3,\,1-p_1]$, and $x\le p_1$ caps
$a\le2p_1$; since $p_1\ge\tfrac14>\tfrac15$ the window is
$[\tfrac{1+p_1}3,\,2p_1]$. Along it $Q$ increases from
$\delta/(2-p_1)<\tfrac13$ \textup{(}as $p_1>\tfrac15$\textup{)} through
$Q=\tfrac13$ at $a_{13}:=\tfrac{1+3p_1}4$ and $Q=\tfrac12$ at
$a_{12}:=\tfrac{1+2p_1}3$, to $Q(2p_1)=p_1/\delta\ge\tfrac12$
\textup{(}as $p_1\ge\tfrac14$; also $a_{13}\le a_{12}\le 2p_1$
there\textup{)}.
nodes.statement_short: Bound by $h(a)$; constraints give the window $[(1+p_1)/3,2p_1]$.

nodes.name: Q <= 1/3
nodes.statement:
\textbf{On $[\tfrac{1+p_1}3,a_{13}]$} ($Q\le\tfrac13$):
$h(a)=J(a)+x+(1-a)C=F(p_1,x)$ with $x\in[\tfrac\delta3,\tfrac{1-p_1}4]$.
Since $\partial_xF=2-C+\log_2\tfrac{x}{1-p_1-x}$ is strictly increasing in
$x$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:fine}), $F$ is decreasing-then-increasing, so
$h\le\max\bigl(F(p_1,\tfrac\delta3),F(p_1,\tfrac{1-p_1}4)\bigr)$.
nodes.statement_short: $h=F(p_1,x)$, maximal at an endpoint.

nodes.name: 1/3 <= Q <= 1/2
nodes.statement:
\textbf{On $[a_{13},a_{12}]$} ($\tfrac13\le Q\le\tfrac12$):
$h\le\max\bigl(\mathrm{fl}(a),\mathrm{co}(a)\bigr)$ pointwise, where
$\mathrm{fl}(a):=J(a)+(1-a)(\tfrac13+C)$ and
$\mathrm{co}(a):=J(a)+(1-a)F_\ell(Q(a))$. Since
$J'=1+\log_2 Q\le1+\log_2\tfrac12=0$ here, $\mathrm{fl}$ is decreasing, and
$\mathrm{fl}(a_{13})=F(p_1,\tfrac{1-p_1}4)$ \textup{(}at $Q=\tfrac13$
the two bounds agree\textup{)}. Expanding $(1-a)F_\ell(Q)$ by the scaled
grouping identity $(1-a)\sum_i \mathrm I(u_i)=\sum_i \mathrm I\bigl(u_i(1-a)\bigr)
-\mathrm I(1-a)$ \textup{(}$\sum_i u_i=1$\textup{)},
\[
  \begin{aligned}
  \mathrm{co}(a)=&(1+a)+\frac{5(1-a)-x}{3}
  +\frac{2(1-a)-x}{3}\,C\\
  &-\mathrm I(p_1)-2\mathrm I(x)\\
  &-\mathrm I\Bigl(\frac{1+2p_1-3a}{3}\Bigr)
  -\mathrm I\Bigl(\frac{2+p_1-3a}{3}\Bigr),
  \end{aligned}
\]
an affine function of $a$ plus terms $-\mathrm I(\text{affine})$, which is
convex. Hence
$\mathrm{co}\le\max\bigl(\mathrm{co}(a_{13}),\mathrm{co}(a_{12})\bigr)$;
$\mathrm{co}(a_{13})\le\mathrm{fl}(a_{13})$ because
$F_\ell(\tfrac13)\le\tfrac13+C$ \textup{(}certificate
\textup{(B1)}\textup{)}, and
$\mathrm{co}(a_{12})=J(a_{12})+(1-a_{12})K=\Theta(p_1)$ by
$F_\ell(\tfrac12)=K$ \textup{(}Lemma~\ref{lem:exact-q}\textup{)}.
nodes.statement_short: Flat and convex pieces bounded by $F(p_1,(1-p_1)/4)$ and $\Theta$.

nodes.name: Q >= 1/2
nodes.statement:
\textbf{On $[a_{12},2p_1]$} ($Q\ge\tfrac12$):
$h\le\max\bigl(\mathrm{fl}_K(a),f(a)\bigr)$ pointwise, where
$\mathrm{fl}_K:=J+(1-a)K$ and $f:=J+(1-a)V(Q)$. $\mathrm{fl}_K$ is convex
($J''>0$), so
$\mathrm{fl}_K\le\max\bigl(\mathrm{fl}_K(a_{12}),\mathrm{fl}_K(2p_1)\bigr)
=\max\bigl(\Theta(p_1),N_K(p_1)\bigr)$. Expanding
$(1-a)\mathrm H_2(Q)=\mathrm I(x)+\mathrm I(1+p_1-2a)-\mathrm I(1-a)$,
\[
  f(a)=3-2a+p_1-\mathrm I(p_1)-2\mathrm I(a-p_1)-\mathrm I(1+p_1-2a),
\]
again convex, so $f\le\max\bigl(f(a_{12}),f(2p_1)\bigr)$; here
$f(a_{12})=J(a_{12})+(1-a_{12})V(\tfrac12)\le\Theta(p_1)$ \textup{(}as
$V(\tfrac12)=\tfrac12<K$\textup{)} and $f(2p_1)=N(p_1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Convex pieces bounded by $\Theta$, $N_K$ and $N$.

nodes.name: Case |L'| = 2
nodes.statement:
If the left part has exactly three symbols, then
\[
  R<\max\bigl(\Pi(p_1),E_1(p_1),E_2(p_1)\bigr).
\]
assumptions: the left part has exactly three symbols
nodes.label: prop:L2-q

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4
nodes.statement:
Here $L'=\{p_2,p_3\}$, $p_3=x-p_2=p_k$, and
$x\,R_{L'}=x\bigl(1-\mathrm H_2(p_2/x)\bigr)$ exactly. Using
$x\,\mathrm H_2(p_2/x)=\mathrm I(p_2)+\mathrm I(p_3)-\mathrm I(x)$, \eqref{eq:master-q} and
Lemma~\ref{lem:msup-q} give
\[
\begin{aligned}
  R\;<\;v(a,p_3):=&(1+a)+x-\mathrm I(p_1)-\mathrm I(1-a)\\
  &-\mathrm I(x-p_3)-\mathrm I(p_3)
  +(1-a)\,M\Bigl(\frac{p_3}{1-a}\Bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]
The constraints are $s\le p_3\le x/2$ \textup{(}Lemma~\ref{lem:key};
$p_3$ is the smaller of the pair\textup{)}, which force
$a\in[\tfrac{2+p_1}5,\tfrac{2-p_1}3]$; the sorting constraint
$p_2\le p_1$ is automatic: for $a\ge\tfrac12$,
$p_2\le x-s=1-p_1-a\le\tfrac12-p_1\le p_1$, and for $a<\tfrac12$,
$p_2\le x-s=3a-1-p_1<\tfrac12-p_1\le p_1$ \textup{(}using

$a\le\tfrac{2-p_1}3<\tfrac{1+p_1}2$ \textup{(}as $p_1>\tfrac15$\textup{)}
we have $x<1-a$, so $p_3/(1-a)\le x/(2(1-a))<\tfrac12$, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:msup-q} gives $M\bigl(p_3/(1-a)\bigr)\le p_3/(1-a)+C$.
Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
  v\;\le\;w(a,p_3):=&(1+a)+x+p_3+(1-a)\,C\\
  &-\mathrm I(p_1)-\mathrm I(1-a)-\mathrm I(x-p_3)-\mathrm I(p_3).
\end{aligned}
\]
For fixed $a$, $w$ is convex in $p_3$, so
$w\le\max\bigl(w(a,s),\,w(a,x/2)\bigr)$.

\textbf{Balanced corner} $w(a,x/2)$. This is convex in $a$ \textup{(}affine plus
$-\mathrm I(1-a)-2\mathrm I(x/2)$\textup{)} on $[\tfrac{2+p_1}5,\tfrac{2-p_1}3]$,
hence at most $\max(E_1,E_2)$, its values at the two endpoints
\textup{(}at $a=\tfrac{2+p_1}5$: $x/2=\tfrac{1-2p_1}5=s$; at
$a=\tfrac{2-p_1}3$: $x/2=\tfrac{1-2p_1}3=s$\textup{)}.

\textbf{Key-tight corner} $w(a,s)$. On $a\le\tfrac12$, $s=1-2a$ and
$x-s=3a-1-p_1$, so $w(a,s)$ is affine plus
$-\mathrm I(1-a)-\mathrm I(3a-1-p_1)-\mathrm I(1-2a)$, hence convex; on
$a\ge\tfrac12$, $s=2a-1$ and $x-s=1-p_1-a$, so it is likewise convex. Hence it
is bounded by its
values at $a\in\{\tfrac{2+p_1}5,\tfrac12,\tfrac{2-p_1}3\}$. The extreme
endpoints coincide with those of the balanced corner \textup{(}there
$s=x/2$\textup{)}, and at $a=\tfrac12$, $s=0$:
$w(\tfrac12,0)=\tfrac32+x+\tfrac{C}2-\mathrm I(p_1)-\mathrm I(\tfrac12)-\mathrm I(x)
=\Pi(p_1)$ with $x=\tfrac12-p_1$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound by $w(a,p_3)$, convex in $p_3$; the balanced and key-tight corners give $E_1,E_2$ and $\Pi$.

nodes.name: Reduce to w(a,p_3)
nodes.statement:
Here $L'=\{p_2,p_3\}$, $p_3=x-p_2=p_k$, and
$x\,R_{L'}=x\bigl(1-\mathrm H_2(p_2/x)\bigr)$ exactly. Using
$x\,\mathrm H_2(p_2/x)=\mathrm I(p_2)+\mathrm I(p_3)-\mathrm I(x)$, \eqref{eq:master-q} and
Lemma~\ref{lem:msup-q} give
\[
\begin{aligned}
  R\;<\;v(a,p_3):=&(1+a)+x-\mathrm I(p_1)-\mathrm I(1-a)\\
  &-\mathrm I(x-p_3)-\mathrm I(p_3)
  +(1-a)\,M\Bigl(\frac{p_3}{1-a}\Bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]
The constraints are $s\le p_3\le x/2$ \textup{(}Lemma~\ref{lem:key};
$p_3$ is the smaller of the pair\textup{)}, which force
$a\in[\tfrac{2+p_1}5,\tfrac{2-p_1}3]$; the sorting constraint
$p_2\le p_1$ is automatic: for $a\ge\tfrac12$,
$p_2\le x-s=1-p_1-a\le\tfrac12-p_1\le p_1$, and for $a<\tfrac12$,
$p_2\le x-s=3a-1-p_1<\tfrac12-p_1\le p_1$ \textup{(}using
$p_1\ge\tfrac14$\textup{)}. Since
$a\le\tfrac{2-p_1}3<\tfrac{1+p_1}2$ \textup{(}as $p_1>\tfrac15$\textup{)}
we have $x<1-a$, so $p_3/(1-a)\le x/(2(1-a))<\tfrac12$, and

Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
  v\;\le\;w(a,p_3):=&(1+a)+x+p_3+(1-a)\,C\\
  &-\mathrm I(p_1)-\mathrm I(1-a)-\mathrm I(x-p_3)-\mathrm I(p_3).
\end{aligned}
\]
For fixed $a$, $w$ is convex in $p_3$, so
$w\le\max\bigl(w(a,s),\,w(a,x/2)\bigr)$.
nodes.statement_short: Exact $L'$ term and the affine right-part bound give $w$, convex in $p_3$.

nodes.name: Balanced corner
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Balanced corner} $w(a,x/2)$. This is convex in $a$ \textup{(}affine plus
$-\mathrm I(1-a)-2\mathrm I(x/2)$\textup{)} on $[\tfrac{2+p_1}5,\tfrac{2-p_1}3]$,
hence at most $\max(E_1,E_2)$, its values at the two endpoints
\textup{(}at $a=\tfrac{2+p_1}5$: $x/2=\tfrac{1-2p_1}5=s$; at
$a=\tfrac{2-p_1}3$: $x/2=\tfrac{1-2p_1}3=s$\textup{)}.
nodes.statement_short: Convex in $a$; endpoint values $E_1,E_2$.

nodes.name: Key-tight corner
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Key-tight corner} $w(a,s)$. On $a\le\tfrac12$, $s=1-2a$ and
$x-s=3a-1-p_1$, so $w(a,s)$ is affine plus
$-\mathrm I(1-a)-\mathrm I(3a-1-p_1)-\mathrm I(1-2a)$, hence convex; on
$a\ge\tfrac12$, $s=2a-1$ and $x-s=1-p_1-a$, so it is likewise convex. Hence it
is bounded by its
values at $a\in\{\tfrac{2+p_1}5,\tfrac12,\tfrac{2-p_1}3\}$. The extreme
endpoints coincide with those of the balanced corner \textup{(}there
$s=x/2$\textup{)}, and at $a=\tfrac12$, $s=0$:
$w(\tfrac12,0)=\tfrac32+x+\tfrac{C}2-\mathrm I(p_1)-\mathrm I(\tfrac12)-\mathrm I(x)
=\Pi(p_1)$ with $x=\tfrac12-p_1$.
nodes.statement_short: Convex on each side of $a=1/2$; value $\Pi(p_1)$ at $a=1/2$.

nodes.name: Case |L'| >= 3
nodes.statement:
If the left part has at least four symbols, then
\[
  R<\max\bigl(\Pi,\Lambda_1,\Lambda_2,\Theta',\Theta''\bigr)(p_1).
\]
assumptions: the left part has at least four symbols
nodes.label: prop:L3-q

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5
nodes.statement:
Now $p_k\le\min\bigl(p_2,\tfrac{x-p_2}2\bigr)\le\tfrac x3$ \textup{(}the
rest $L'\setminus\{p_2\}$ has $\ge2$ symbols, each $\ge p_k$\textup{)}, so
the constraint $s\le p_k\le x/3$ confines
$a\in[\tfrac{3+p_1}7,\tfrac{3-p_1}5]$, whence $1-a\ge\tfrac{2+p_1}5$ and
$p_k/(1-a)\le\tfrac{x/3}{1-a}\le\tfrac{1-2p_1}{2+p_1}<\tfrac13$
\textup{(}as $p_1>\tfrac17$\textup{)}: the right part is always bounded
affinely, $(1-a)R_B<p_k+(1-a)\,C$. The redundancy of $L'$ is bounded by
$x\,\mathrm{ch}(q')$, $q':=p_2/x$. Since the total is increasing in
$p_k$, put $p_k=\min\bigl(p_2,\tfrac{x-p_2}2\bigr)$ and write
$D(a):=J(a)+(1-a)\,C$.

\textbf{Branch $p_2\le x/3$} \textup{(}$p_k=p_2$, $q'\le\tfrac13$;
Lemma~\ref{lem:msup-q} gives $\mathrm{ch}(q')\le q'+C$ there\textup{)}:
the total is at most $D+2p_2+xC$, increasing in $p_2$, hence at most
$\Lambda(a):=D(a)+\tfrac{2x}3+xC$, which is convex in $a$
\textup{(}$J''>0$\textup{)}, so $\Lambda\le\max(\Lambda_1,\Lambda_2)$,
its endpoint values at $x=\tfrac{3\delta}7$ and $x=\tfrac{3\delta}5$.

\textbf{Branch $p_2\ge x/3$} \textup{(}$p_k=\tfrac{x-p_2}2$\textup{)}: the
total is $g(p_2):=D(a)+x\,\mathrm{ch}(q')+\tfrac{x-p_2}2$ with
$p_2\in[\tfrac x3,\,x-2s]$ \textup{(}the ceiling from
$p_k\ge s$\textup{)}; note $q'\le q'_{\max}:=1-2s/x$, and $q'\ge\tfrac12$
occurs \textup{(}iff $p_2\ge x/2$\textup{)} only when $s\le x/4$. Bound
$\mathrm{ch}$ by its three regime forms; each resulting expression is
convex (or monotone) in $p_2$:
the form $D+x(\tfrac13+C)+\tfrac{x-p_2}2$ \textup{(}valid for
$q'\in[\tfrac13,\tfrac12)$ via $W_{\mathrm{iso}}\le\tfrac13+C$, as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:msup-q}\textup{)} is decreasing in $p_2$, hence at most its
value $\Lambda(a)$ at $p_2=\tfrac x3$; the form
$D+xF_\ell(p_2/x)+\tfrac{x-p_2}2$ is convex in $p_2$ \textup{(}the scaled
$xF_\ell(p_2/x)$ has $\mathrm I$-arguments $p_2,\tfrac{x-2p_2}3,\tfrac{2x-p_2}3$,
affine in $p_2$\textup{)}, with maximum at $p_2=\tfrac x3$ \textup{(}where
\textup{(B1)} gives $\le\Lambda(a)$\textup{)} or at
$p_2=\min(\tfrac x2,x-2s)$; the form with $V(q')$
\textup{(}$q'\ge\tfrac12$, so $s\le x/4$\textup{)} is convex in $p_2$ via
$xV(p_2/x)=2x-p_2-\mathrm I(p_2)-\mathrm I(x-p_2)+\mathrm I(x)$, with maximum at
$p_2=\tfrac x2$ \textup{(}value $\le D+xK+\tfrac x4$, as
$V(\tfrac12)=\tfrac12<K$\textup{)} or at $p_2=x-2s$. Three corner curves
in $a$ remain.

\textbf{(a) The half corner} $\kappa_0(a):=D(a)+xK+\tfrac x4$ \textup{(}from
$p_2=\tfrac x2$; by $F_\ell(\tfrac12)=K$ it also dominates the
$F_\ell$-bound there\textup{)}, defined for $s\le\tfrac x4$, i.e.\
$a\in[\tfrac{4+p_1}9,\tfrac{4-p_1}7]$. It is convex, so
$\kappa_0\le\max(\Theta'',\Theta')$, its endpoint values.

\textbf{(b) The Key-tight corner with $q'_{\max}<\tfrac12$}
\textup{(}$p_2=x-2s$, $\tfrac x4\le s\le\tfrac x3$\textup{)}: the
expression $D+xF_\ell(1-2s/x)+s$ has $\mathrm I$-arguments
$x-2s,\ \tfrac{4s-x}3,\ \tfrac{x+2s}3$, all affine in $a$ on either side
of $a=\tfrac12$, hence convex there; and its window endpoints are $s=\tfrac x3$
\textup{(}$q'_{\max}=\tfrac13$, value $\le\Lambda(a)$ by
\textup{(B1)}\textup{)} and $s=\tfrac x4$ \textup{(}$q'_{\max}=\tfrac12$,
value $=\kappa_0$ at the corresponding endpoint\textup{)}. Sorting is
inactive here: $p_2=x-2s\le\tfrac x2\le\tfrac{3\delta}{10}<\tfrac14\le p_1$.

\textbf{(c) The Key-tight corner with $q'_{\max}\ge\tfrac12$}
\textup{(}$p_2=x-2s$, $s\le\tfrac x4$, $V$-bound\textup{)}:
\[
\begin{aligned}
  m(a)\;=\;&(1+a)-\mathrm I(p_1)-\mathrm I(1-a)\\
  &+(1-a)\,C+x+3s-\mathrm I(x-2s)-\mathrm I(2s),
\end{aligned}
\]
convex on either side of $a=\tfrac12$; its corners are $a=\tfrac12$, where
$s=0$ and $m=\Pi(p_1)$ exactly, and $s=\tfrac x4$, where
$2\mathrm I(\tfrac x2)=x+\mathrm I(x)$ gives
$m=\kappa_0-x\bigl(K-\tfrac12\bigr)\le\kappa_0$. Sorting is again
inactive: over this branch $p_2=x-2s$ is maximised at $a=\tfrac12$, where
it equals $\tfrac12-p_1\le p_1$.
nodes.statement_short: Affine right-part bound, then a branch split on $p_2$ versus $x/3$; three corner curves remain, each convex, bounded at endpoints.

nodes.name: Window and right-part bound
nodes.statement:
Now $p_k\le\min\bigl(p_2,\tfrac{x-p_2}2\bigr)\le\tfrac x3$ \textup{(}the
rest $L'\setminus\{p_2\}$ has $\ge2$ symbols, each $\ge p_k$\textup{)}, so
the constraint $s\le p_k\le x/3$ confines
$a\in[\tfrac{3+p_1}7,\tfrac{3-p_1}5]$, whence $1-a\ge\tfrac{2+p_1}5$ and
$p_k/(1-a)\le\tfrac{x/3}{1-a}\le\tfrac{1-2p_1}{2+p_1}<\tfrac13$
\textup{(}as $p_1>\tfrac17$\textup{)}: the right part is always bounded
affinely, $(1-a)R_B<p_k+(1-a)\,C$. The redundancy of $L'$ is bounded by
$x\,\mathrm{ch}(q')$, $q':=p_2/x$. Since the total is increasing in
$p_k$, put $p_k=\min\bigl(p_2,\tfrac{x-p_2}2\bigr)$ and write
$D(a):=J(a)+(1-a)\,C$.
nodes.statement_short: Constraints confine $a$; right part bounded affinely; set $D(a)$.

nodes.name: Branch p_2 <= x/3
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Branch $p_2\le x/3$} \textup{(}$p_k=p_2$, $q'\le\tfrac13$;
Lemma~\ref{lem:msup-q} gives $\mathrm{ch}(q')\le q'+C$ there\textup{)}:
the total is at most $D+2p_2+xC$, increasing in $p_2$, hence at most
$\Lambda(a):=D(a)+\tfrac{2x}3+xC$, which is convex in $a$
\textup{(}$J''>0$\textup{)}, so $\Lambda\le\max(\Lambda_1,\Lambda_2)$,
its endpoint values at $x=\tfrac{3\delta}7$ and $x=\tfrac{3\delta}5$.
nodes.statement_short: Bounded by $\Lambda(a)\le\max(\Lambda_1,\Lambda_2)$.

nodes.name: Branch p_2 >= x/3
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Branch $p_2\ge x/3$} \textup{(}$p_k=\tfrac{x-p_2}2$\textup{)}: the
total is $g(p_2):=D(a)+x\,\mathrm{ch}(q')+\tfrac{x-p_2}2$ with
$p_2\in[\tfrac x3,\,x-2s]$ \textup{(}the ceiling from
$p_k\ge s$\textup{)}; note $q'\le q'_{\max}:=1-2s/x$, and $q'\ge\tfrac12$
occurs \textup{(}iff $p_2\ge x/2$\textup{)} only when $s\le x/4$. Bound
$\mathrm{ch}$ by its three regime forms; each resulting expression is
convex (or monotone) in $p_2$:
the form $D+x(\tfrac13+C)+\tfrac{x-p_2}2$ \textup{(}valid for
$q'\in[\tfrac13,\tfrac12)$ via $W_{\mathrm{iso}}\le\tfrac13+C$, as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:msup-q}\textup{)} is decreasing in $p_2$, hence at most its
value $\Lambda(a)$ at $p_2=\tfrac x3$; the form
$D+xF_\ell(p_2/x)+\tfrac{x-p_2}2$ is convex in $p_2$ \textup{(}the scaled
$xF_\ell(p_2/x)$ has $\mathrm I$-arguments $p_2,\tfrac{x-2p_2}3,\tfrac{2x-p_2}3$,
affine in $p_2$\textup{)}, with maximum at $p_2=\tfrac x3$ \textup{(}where
\textup{(B1)} gives $\le\Lambda(a)$\textup{)} or at
$p_2=\min(\tfrac x2,x-2s)$; the form with $V(q')$
\textup{(}$q'\ge\tfrac12$, so $s\le x/4$\textup{)} is convex in $p_2$ via
$xV(p_2/x)=2x-p_2-\mathrm I(p_2)-\mathrm I(x-p_2)+\mathrm I(x)$, with maximum at
$p_2=\tfrac x2$ \textup{(}value $\le D+xK+\tfrac x4$, as
$V(\tfrac12)=\tfrac12<K$\textup{)} or at $p_2=x-2s$. Three corner curves
in $a$ remain.
nodes.statement_short: Regime forms of ch reduce to three corner curves.

nodes.name: (a) half corner
nodes.statement:
\textbf{(a) The half corner} $\kappa_0(a):=D(a)+xK+\tfrac x4$ \textup{(}from
$p_2=\tfrac x2$; by $F_\ell(\tfrac12)=K$ it also dominates the
$F_\ell$-bound there\textup{)}, defined for $s\le\tfrac x4$, i.e.\
$a\in[\tfrac{4+p_1}9,\tfrac{4-p_1}7]$. It is convex, so
$\kappa_0\le\max(\Theta'',\Theta')$, its endpoint values.
nodes.statement_short: Convex; bounded by $\Theta',\Theta''$.

nodes.name: (b) key-tight corner, q'_max < 1/2
nodes.statement:
\textbf{(b) The Key-tight corner with $q'_{\max}<\tfrac12$}
\textup{(}$p_2=x-2s$, $\tfrac x4\le s\le\tfrac x3$\textup{)}: the
expression $D+xF_\ell(1-2s/x)+s$ has $\mathrm I$-arguments
$x-2s,\ \tfrac{4s-x}3,\ \tfrac{x+2s}3$, all affine in $a$ on either side
of $a=\tfrac12$, hence convex there; and its window endpoints are $s=\tfrac x3$
\textup{(}$q'_{\max}=\tfrac13$, value $\le\Lambda(a)$ by
\textup{(B1)}\textup{)} and $s=\tfrac x4$ \textup{(}$q'_{\max}=\tfrac12$,
value $=\kappa_0$ at the corresponding endpoint\textup{)}. Sorting is
inactive here: $p_2=x-2s\le\tfrac x2\le\tfrac{3\delta}{10}<\tfrac14\le p_1$.
nodes.statement_short: Convex; endpoints bounded by $\Lambda$ and $\kappa_0$.

nodes.name: (c) key-tight corner, q'_max >= 1/2
nodes.statement:
\textbf{(c) The Key-tight corner with $q'_{\max}\ge\tfrac12$}
\textup{(}$p_2=x-2s$, $s\le\tfrac x4$, $V$-bound\textup{)}:
\[
\begin{aligned}
  m(a)\;=\;&(1+a)-\mathrm I(p_1)-\mathrm I(1-a)\\
  &+(1-a)\,C+x+3s-\mathrm I(x-2s)-\mathrm I(2s),
\end{aligned}
\]
convex on either side of $a=\tfrac12$; its corners are $a=\tfrac12$, where
$s=0$ and $m=\Pi(p_1)$ exactly, and $s=\tfrac x4$, where
$2\mathrm I(\tfrac x2)=x+\mathrm I(x)$ gives
$m=\kappa_0-x\bigl(K-\tfrac12\bigr)\le\kappa_0$. Sorting is again
inactive: over this branch $p_2=x-2s$ is maximised at $a=\tfrac12$, where
it equals $\tfrac12-p_1\le p_1$.
nodes.statement_short: Convex; corners give $\Pi$ and at most $\kappa_0$.

nodes.name: All corners under three curves
nodes.statement_short: On $[1/4,1/3]$ every corner curve is dominated by $\Theta$ or $\Pi$.
nodes.label: lem:dom-q

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 18
nodes.statement:
Every difference is affine in $p_1$ plus terms $\pm \mathrm I(u(p_1))$ with $u$
affine; second derivatives are computed as in Lemma~\ref{lem:midcomp}, and
endpoint signs are Lemmas~\ref{lem:exact-q} and~\ref{lem:cert-q}.

\textup{(a)} $\Theta-F(\cdot,\tfrac\delta3)$: second derivative
$\bigl[\tfrac1{1-p_1}-\tfrac4{3\delta}-\tfrac1{3(2-p_1)}\bigr]/\ln2<0$
\textup{(}$\delta\le\tfrac12$ gives $\tfrac4{3\delta}\ge\tfrac83$ while
$\tfrac1{1-p_1}\le\tfrac32$\textup{)}, so concave, and $\ge0$ at both ends
\textup{(}\textup{(C1)} at $\tfrac14$; $0$ exactly at $\tfrac13$, the
contact of Lemma~\ref{lem:exact-q}\textup{)}, hence $\ge0$ between.
$\Theta-F(\cdot,\tfrac{1-\cdot}4)$ is affine
(Lemma~\ref{lem:exact-q}) and positive at both ends
\textup{(}\textup{(C2)}\textup{)}. $\Theta-N_K$: second derivative
$\bigl[\tfrac1{1-p_1}-\tfrac1{p_1}-\tfrac4\delta\bigr]/\ln2<0$, so concave;
it vanishes exactly at $\tfrac14$ \textup{(}both values
$\tfrac{1+C}4$\textup{)} and is positive at $\tfrac13$
\textup{(}\textup{(C3)}\textup{)}.

\textup{(b)} $\Pi'=-1+\log_2\tfrac{p_1}{1/2-p_1}\le0$ iff
$p_1\le2\bigl(\tfrac12-p_1\bigr)$, i.e.\ $p_1\le\tfrac13$. Each of
$E_1,E_2,\Lambda_1,\Theta''$ is convex, so bounded by the larger of its
values at $p_1\in\{\tfrac14,\tfrac13\}$, and all eight values are below
$\Pi(\tfrac13)$: \textup{(D1)}--\textup{(D4)}.

\textup{(c)} $\Pi-\Lambda_2$: the terms $-\mathrm I(p_1)$ cancel; the second
derivative is
$\bigl[\tfrac2\delta-\tfrac{12}{5\delta}-\tfrac1{5(2+p_1)}\bigr]/\ln2
=\bigl[-\tfrac2{5\delta}-\tfrac1{5(2+p_1)}\bigr]/\ln2<0$, so concave and
positive at both ends \textup{(}\textup{(D5)}\textup{)}. $\Pi-\Theta'$:
second derivative
$\bigl[\tfrac2\delta-\tfrac{16}{7\delta}-\tfrac1{7(3+p_1)}\bigr]/\ln2<0$,
so concave and positive at both ends \textup{(}\textup{(D6)}\textup{)}.
nodes.statement_short: Second-derivative signs plus certified endpoint values (Lemmas 14, 15).

nodes.name: Method
nodes.statement:
Every difference is affine in $p_1$ plus terms $\pm \mathrm I(u(p_1))$ with $u$
affine; second derivatives are computed as in Lemma~\ref{lem:midcomp}, and

nodes.name: (a)
nodes.statement:
\textup{(a)} $\Theta-F(\cdot,\tfrac\delta3)$: second derivative
$\bigl[\tfrac1{1-p_1}-\tfrac4{3\delta}-\tfrac1{3(2-p_1)}\bigr]/\ln2<0$
\textup{(}$\delta\le\tfrac12$ gives $\tfrac4{3\delta}\ge\tfrac83$ while
$\tfrac1{1-p_1}\le\tfrac32$\textup{)}, so concave, and $\ge0$ at both ends
\textup{(}\textup{(C1)} at $\tfrac14$; $0$ exactly at $\tfrac13$, the

$\bigl[\tfrac1{1-p_1}-\tfrac1{p_1}-\tfrac4\delta\bigr]/\ln2<0$, so concave;
it vanishes exactly at $\tfrac14$ \textup{(}both values

nodes.name: (b)
nodes.statement:
\textup{(b)} $\Pi'=-1+\log_2\tfrac{p_1}{1/2-p_1}\le0$ iff
$p_1\le2\bigl(\tfrac12-p_1\bigr)$, i.e.\ $p_1\le\tfrac13$. Each of
$E_1,E_2,\Lambda_1,\Theta''$ is convex, so bounded by the larger of its
values at $p_1\in\{\tfrac14,\tfrac13\}$, and all eight values are below
$\Pi(\tfrac13)$: \textup{(D1)}--\textup{(D4)}.
nodes.statement_short: $\Pi$ decreasing; convex curves below $\Pi(1/3)$ by (D1)-(D4).

nodes.name: (c)
nodes.statement:
\textup{(c)} $\Pi-\Lambda_2$: the terms $-\mathrm I(p_1)$ cancel; the second
derivative is
$\bigl[\tfrac2\delta-\tfrac{12}{5\delta}-\tfrac1{5(2+p_1)}\bigr]/\ln2
=\bigl[-\tfrac2{5\delta}-\tfrac1{5(2+p_1)}\bigr]/\ln2<0$, so concave and
positive at both ends \textup{(}\textup{(D5)}\textup{)}. $\Pi-\Theta'$:
second derivative
$\bigl[\tfrac2\delta-\tfrac{16}{7\delta}-\tfrac1{7(3+p_1)}\bigr]/\ln2<0$,

nodes.statement_short: Concave differences positive at both ends by (D5), (D6).

nodes.name: Single crossings
nodes.statement:
On $[\tfrac14,\tfrac13]$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textup{(i)}] $\Pi-\Theta$ is convex, equals $\tfrac{C}4>0$ at
$\tfrac14$ and is negative at $\tfrac13$
\textup{(}\textup{(A1)}\textup{)}; hence it has a unique zero $b_1$, is
$\ge0$ before and $\le0$ after.
\item[\textup{(ii)}] $\Theta-N$ is concave, equals $\tfrac{C}4>0$ at
$\tfrac14$ and is negative at $\tfrac13$
\textup{(}\textup{(A2)}\textup{)}; hence it has a unique zero $b_2$, is
$\ge0$ before and $\le0$ after.
\item[\textup{(iii)}] $b_1<b_2$: at $\rho=\tfrac{23}{72}$ both
$\Theta-\Pi>0$ and $\Theta-N>0$ hold \textup{(}\textup{(S)}\textup{)},
so $b_1<\rho<b_2$.
\end{enumerate}
Numerically $b_1=0.3190251\ldots$, $b_2=0.3196323\ldots$
conclusions: hence it has a unique zero $b_1$
hence it has a unique zero $b_2$
nodes.statement_short: $\Pi-\Theta$ and $\Theta-N$ each change sign exactly once on $[1/4,1/3]$, at $b_1<b_2$.
nodes.label: lem:cross-q

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 19
nodes.statement:
$(\Pi-\Theta)''\ln2=\tfrac1{1/2-p_1}-\tfrac1{1-p_1}>0$ \textup{(}the
$-\mathrm I(p_1)$ terms cancel; the $\Theta$-terms contribute
$-\tfrac1{3(1-p_1)}-\tfrac2{3(1-p_1)}$\textup{)}, and
$(\Theta-N)''\ln2=\tfrac1{1-p_1}-\tfrac2{p_1}-\tfrac9{1-3p_1}<0$. The
values at $\tfrac14$ are Lemma~\ref{lem:exact-q}. A convex function
positive at $\tfrac14$ and negative at $\tfrac13$ has exactly one zero
there with the stated sign pattern (its derivative changes sign at most
once); likewise the concave difference in (ii). For (iii), the two
certified signs at $\rho$ place $\rho$ strictly between the zeros.
nodes.statement_short: Convexity/concavity from second derivatives, endpoint signs from Lemmas 14 and 15, and a certified point between the zeros.

nodes.name: Second derivatives
nodes.statement:
$(\Pi-\Theta)''\ln2=\tfrac1{1/2-p_1}-\tfrac1{1-p_1}>0$ \textup{(}the
$-\mathrm I(p_1)$ terms cancel; the $\Theta$-terms contribute
$-\tfrac1{3(1-p_1)}-\tfrac2{3(1-p_1)}$\textup{)}, and
$(\Theta-N)''\ln2=\tfrac1{1-p_1}-\tfrac2{p_1}-\tfrac9{1-3p_1}<0$.
nodes.statement_short: Compute the second derivatives of both differences.

nodes.name: Endpoint values
nodes.statement:
The
values at $\tfrac14$ are Lemma~\ref{lem:exact-q}.
nodes.statement_short: Values at $1/4$ from Lemma 14.

nodes.name: Unique zeros
nodes.statement:
A convex function
positive at $\tfrac14$ and negative at $\tfrac13$ has exactly one zero
there with the stated sign pattern (its derivative changes sign at most
once); likewise the concave difference in (ii).
nodes.statement_short: Sign change of a convex/concave function is unique.
