nodes.name: Quarter-window ceiling
nodes.statement:
Let $\tfrac14\le p_1<\tfrac13$. Then, with $b_1<b_2$ as in
Lemma~\textup{\ref{lem:cross-q}},
\[
  R\;<\;W_3(p_1)\;:=\;
  \begin{cases}
    \ \Pi(p_1), & \tfrac14\le p_1\le b_1,\\[3pt]
    \ \Theta(p_1), & b_1\le p_1\le b_2,\\[3pt]
    \ N(p_1), & b_2\le p_1<\tfrac13 .
  \end{cases}
\]
Equivalently $R<\max(\Pi,\Theta,N)(p_1)$; the piecewise identification
holds because $\Pi\ge\Theta$ iff $p_1\le b_1$ and $\Theta\ge N$ iff
$p_1\le b_2$.
nodes.statement_short: For $p_1\in[1/4,1/3)$, $R<\max(\Pi,\Theta,N)(p_1)$, the three pieces switching at $b_1<b_2$.
nodes.label: thm:quarter

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4
nodes.statement:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:noburial-q} every source in the regime satisfies
\eqref{eq:master-q}, and by
Propositions~\ref{prop:L1-q}--\ref{prop:L3-q} (the three possible sizes
of $L'$),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  R\;<\;\max\Bigl\{&F\bigl(\cdot,\tfrac\delta3\bigr),
  F\bigl(\cdot,\tfrac{1-\cdot}4\bigr),\Theta,N_K,N,\\
  &\ \Pi,E_1,E_2,\Lambda_1,\Lambda_2,\Theta',\Theta''\Bigr\}(p_1).
\end{aligned}
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:dom-q} every listed curve except $\Pi,\Theta,N$ is
dominated by $\Theta$ or by $\Pi$ on all of $[\tfrac14,\tfrac13]$, so
$R<\max(\Pi,\Theta,N)$; Lemma~\ref{lem:cross-q} identifies the maximum
piecewise.
nodes.statement_short: No-burial identity plus the three size cases of $L'$, then domination of all corner curves by $\Pi,\Theta,N$.

nodes.name: Domination of the affine bound on [1/4,1/3)
nodes.statement:
On $[\tfrac14,\tfrac13)$, $W_3(p_1)<p_1+C$, with margin at least
$\tfrac13+C-(2-\log_23)=0.04841\ldots$ \textup{(}\textup{(A3)}\textup{)}
and as much as $0.176$ near $p_1\approx0.3196$. Moreover
$W_3(\tfrac14)=\tfrac14+\tfrac{C}2$ \textup{(}half the affine constant
is removed at the left endpoint\textup{)}, and
$\sup_{[\frac14,\frac13)}W_3=(2-\log_23)^-$.
nodes.statement_short: On $[1/4,1/3)$ the quarter-window ceiling is strictly below $p_1+C$, by at least $0.0484$.
nodes.label: prop:dom-q

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6
nodes.statement:
On $[\tfrac14,b_1]$: $p_1+C-\Pi$ has derivative
$2-\log_2\tfrac{p_1}{1/2-p_1}\ge2-\log_22>0$, so the margin is minimised at
$\tfrac14$, value $\tfrac{C}2$. On $[b_1,b_2]$: $p_1+C-\Theta$ is
concave \textup{(}$\Theta$ is convex\textup{)}, positive at $\tfrac14$
\textup{(}$\tfrac34C$\textup{)} and at $\tfrac13$ \textup{(}since
$\Theta(\tfrac13)<N(\tfrac13^-)=2-\log_23$ by \textup{(A2)}, it exceeds
$\tfrac13+C-(2-\log_23)>0$\textup{)}. On $[b_2,\tfrac13)$: $p_1+C-N$ has
derivative $1-N'=4+3\log_2\tfrac{1-3p_1}{p_1}$, and on
$[b_2,\tfrac13)\subset[\rho,\tfrac13)$ one has
$\tfrac{1-3p_1}{p_1}\le\tfrac{1-3\rho}{\rho}=\tfrac3{23}<2^{-4/3}$, so the margin
decreases to the limit $\tfrac13+C-(2-\log_23)>0$ at $\tfrac13^-$
\textup{(}\textup{(A3)}\textup{)}. Finally $W_3$ increases to
$N(\tfrac13^-)=2-\log_23$ along the third piece \textup{(}there
$N'=-3+3\log_2\tfrac{p_1}{1-3p_1}>0$, since $p_1>2(1-3p_1)$ for
$p_1>\tfrac27$\textup{)}, while on the first two pieces
$W_3\le\Pi(\tfrac14)<2-\log_23$ \textup{(}$\Pi$ decreasing; on $[b_1,b_2]$,
$\Theta\le\max\bigl(\Theta(b_1),\Theta(b_2)\bigr)
=\max\bigl(\Pi(b_1),N(b_2)\bigr)$; and \textup{(A3)}\textup{)}.
nodes.statement_short: Piece by piece: monotone or concave margins evaluated at endpoints, with certificate (A3).

nodes.name: Pi piece
nodes.statement:
On $[\tfrac14,b_1]$: $p_1+C-\Pi$ has derivative
$2-\log_2\tfrac{p_1}{1/2-p_1}\ge2-\log_22>0$, so the margin is minimised at
$\tfrac14$, value $\tfrac{C}2$.
nodes.statement_short: Margin increasing; minimum $C/2$ at $1/4$.

nodes.name: Theta piece
nodes.statement:
On $[b_1,b_2]$: $p_1+C-\Theta$ is
concave \textup{(}$\Theta$ is convex\textup{)}, positive at $\tfrac14$
\textup{(}$\tfrac34C$\textup{)} and at $\tfrac13$ \textup{(}since
$\Theta(\tfrac13)<N(\tfrac13^-)=2-\log_23$ by \textup{(A2)}, it exceeds
$\tfrac13+C-(2-\log_23)>0$\textup{)}.
nodes.statement_short: Concave margin, positive at both ends.

nodes.name: N piece
nodes.statement:
On $[b_2,\tfrac13)$: $p_1+C-N$ has
derivative $1-N'=4+3\log_2\tfrac{1-3p_1}{p_1}$, and on
$[b_2,\tfrac13)\subset[\rho,\tfrac13)$ one has
$\tfrac{1-3p_1}{p_1}\le\tfrac{1-3\rho}{\rho}=\tfrac3{23}<2^{-4/3}$, so the margin
decreases to the limit $\tfrac13+C-(2-\log_23)>0$ at $\tfrac13^-$
\textup{(}\textup{(A3)}\textup{)}.
nodes.statement_short: Margin decreases to the positive limit (A3).

nodes.name: Supremum of W_3
nodes.statement:
Finally $W_3$ increases to
$N(\tfrac13^-)=2-\log_23$ along the third piece \textup{(}there
$N'=-3+3\log_2\tfrac{p_1}{1-3p_1}>0$, since $p_1>2(1-3p_1)$ for
$p_1>\tfrac27$\textup{)}, while on the first two pieces
$W_3\le\Pi(\tfrac14)<2-\log_23$ \textup{(}$\Pi$ decreasing; on $[b_1,b_2]$,
$\Theta\le\max\bigl(\Theta(b_1),\Theta(b_2)\bigr)
=\max\bigl(\Pi(b_1),N(b_2)\bigr)$; and \textup{(A3)}\textup{)}.
nodes.statement_short: $W_3$ increases to $2-\log_2 3$ on the last piece.

nodes.name: The top piece is exact
nodes.statement:
For every $p_1\in[b_2,\tfrac13)$,
\[
  \sup\{R(p): p\text{ a source with largest symbol }p_1\}=N(p_1);
\]
the supremum is approached but not attained. For every
$p_1\in[\tfrac14,\tfrac13)$ the family in the proof shows the supremum is at
least $N(p_1)$.
conclusions: \sup\{R(p): p\text{ a source with largest symbol }p_1\}=N(p_1)
the supremum is approached but not attained
nodes.statement_short: On $[b_2,1/3)$ the $N$ branch is the exact supremum of $R$ given $p_1$ (not attained).
nodes.label: prop:tight-q

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 7
nodes.statement:
Fix $p_1\in[\tfrac14,\tfrac13)$ and $0<\varepsilon<\tfrac12$, and consider
\[
  p^{(\varepsilon)}
  =\bigl(p_1,p_1,p_1,(1-3p_1)(1-\varepsilon),(1-3p_1)\varepsilon\bigr).
\]
It is sorted because $1-3p_1\le p_1$. The root prefix imbalances at the first
three cuts are
\[
  1-2p_1,\qquad |4p_1-1|,\qquad 6p_1-1,
\]
and the second is minimal for $\tfrac14\le p_1<\tfrac13$; the fourth cut has
imbalance $1-2(1-3p_1)\varepsilon\ge\tfrac12$, while
$|4p_1-1|\le\tfrac13$. Thus the root split is
$(p_1,p_1)\,|\,(p_1,(1-3p_1)(1-\varepsilon),(1-3p_1)\varepsilon)$. The left
child has zero redundancy. In the right child the leader fraction is
$p_1/(1-2p_1)\ge\tfrac12$, so it isolates; the remaining pair has redundancy
$1-\mathrm H_2(\varepsilon)$. Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:rec} twice gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
  R(p^{(\varepsilon)})
  =\ &1-\mathrm H_2(2p_1)\\
  &+(1-2p_1)\Bigl(1-\mathrm H_2\Bigl(\frac{p_1}{1-2p_1}\Bigr)\Bigr)\\
  &+(1-3p_1)\bigl(1-\mathrm H_2(\varepsilon)\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]
Letting $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ and grouping entropy terms,
\[
  R(p^{(\varepsilon)})\longrightarrow
  3-3p_1-\mathrm H(p_1,p_1,p_1,1-3p_1)=N(p_1).
\]
For $p_1\in[b_2,\tfrac13)$, Theorem~\ref{thm:quarter} gives the matching
strict upper bound $R<N(p_1)$ for every finite source, so the supremum is
exactly $N(p_1)$ and is not attained.
nodes.statement_short: Explicit five-symbol family $p^{(\varepsilon)}$ whose redundancy tends to $N(p_1)$; matching upper bound from Theorem 4.

nodes.name: Extremal family
nodes.statement:
Fix $p_1\in[\tfrac14,\tfrac13)$ and $0<\varepsilon<\tfrac12$, and consider
\[
  p^{(\varepsilon)}
  =\bigl(p_1,p_1,p_1,(1-3p_1)(1-\varepsilon),(1-3p_1)\varepsilon\bigr).
\]
It is sorted because $1-3p_1\le p_1$.
nodes.statement_short: Construct the sorted family $p^{(\varepsilon)}$.

nodes.name: Root split
nodes.statement:
The root prefix imbalances at the first
three cuts are
\[
  1-2p_1,\qquad |4p_1-1|,\qquad 6p_1-1,
\]
and the second is minimal for $\tfrac14\le p_1<\tfrac13$; the fourth cut has
imbalance $1-2(1-3p_1)\varepsilon\ge\tfrac12$, while
$|4p_1-1|\le\tfrac13$. Thus the root split is
$(p_1,p_1)\,|\,(p_1,(1-3p_1)(1-\varepsilon),(1-3p_1)\varepsilon)$.
nodes.statement_short: Compare cut imbalances: the root split is $(p_1,p_1)|(\dots)$.

nodes.name: Children
nodes.statement:
The left
child has zero redundancy. In the right child the leader fraction is
$p_1/(1-2p_1)\ge\tfrac12$, so it isolates; the remaining pair has redundancy
$1-\mathrm H_2(\varepsilon)$.
nodes.statement_short: Left child redundancy 0; right child isolates its leader.

nodes.name: Limit
nodes.statement:
Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:rec} twice gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
  R(p^{(\varepsilon)})
  =\ &1-\mathrm H_2(2p_1)\\
  &+(1-2p_1)\Bigl(1-\mathrm H_2\Bigl(\frac{p_1}{1-2p_1}\Bigr)\Bigr)\\
  &+(1-3p_1)\bigl(1-\mathrm H_2(\varepsilon)\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]
Letting $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ and grouping entropy terms,
\[
  R(p^{(\varepsilon)})\longrightarrow
  3-3p_1-\mathrm H(p_1,p_1,p_1,1-3p_1)=N(p_1).
\]
nodes.statement_short: Recursion twice and $\varepsilon\to0$ give $N(p_1)$.

nodes.name: Matching upper bound
nodes.statement:
For $p_1\in[b_2,\tfrac13)$, Theorem~\ref{thm:quarter} gives the matching
strict upper bound $R<N(p_1)$ for every finite source, so the supremum is
exactly $N(p_1)$ and is not attained.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 4 gives $R<N(p_1)$, so the supremum is exact and not attained.

nodes.name: Point and interval inequalities
nodes.statement:
Every inequality between explicit constants in this paper is of one of two
kinds. The \emph{point} inequalities (the values of Lemma~\ref{lem:exact-q} and
the certificates of Lemma~\ref{lem:cert-q}) are signs of constants. The
\emph{interval} inequalities (the domination steps of
Appendices~\ref{sec:affine}, \ref{sec:midcap}, and~\ref{sec:quarter}) compare
two functions on an interval and are reduced to endpoint values, but only after
the sign of a second derivative is computed.
nodes.statement_short: Point inequalities are signs of constants; interval inequalities compare functions on an interval via endpoints after a second-derivative sign.

nodes.name: Certification method
nodes.statement:
\textup{(i)} A constant $c_0+\sum_i c_i\log_2 m_i$ with $c_i\in\mathbb Q$ and
$m_i\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$ has a sign decided by finitely many comparisons of integer
powers, since $\log_2 m\gtrless\tfrac ab\iff m^{\,b}\gtrless 2^{\,a}$; and
$\mathrm I(a/b)=\tfrac ab(\log_2 b-\log_2 a)$, so any of the curves evaluated at a
rational point is of this form.

\textup{(ii)} Let $g(x)=\ell(x)+\sum_j c_j\,\mathrm I\bigl(u_j(x)\bigr)$ on
$[\alpha,\beta]$, with $\ell$ and the $u_j$ affine, $c_j\in\mathbb Q$, and
$u_j>0$. Then
\[
  g''(x)\;=\;-\frac1{\ln2}\sum_j\frac{c_j\,s_j^{\,2}}{u_j(x)},
  \qquad s_j:=u_j'.
\]
If $g''\le0$ throughout $[\alpha,\beta]$ then $g$ is concave and
$g\ge\min\{g(\alpha),g(\beta)\}$; if $g''\ge0$ throughout then $g$ is convex and
$g\le\max\{g(\alpha),g(\beta)\}$. The endpoint values are constants of the form
in \textup{(i)}.
conclusions:
has a sign decided by finitely many comparisons of integer
powers

If $g''\le0$ throughout $[\alpha,\beta]$ then $g$ is concave and
$g\ge\min\{g(\alpha),g(\beta)\}$; if $g''\ge0$ throughout then $g$ is convex and
$g\le\max\{g(\alpha),g(\beta)\}$
nodes.statement_short: Signs of rational log-combinations reduce to integer power comparisons; affine-plus-entropy functions have explicit second derivatives giving endpoint bounds.
nodes.label: lem:certify

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 20
nodes.statement:
\textup{(i)} is the two displayed identities. \textup{(ii)}:
$\mathrm I(u)=-u\log_2 u$ has $\mathrm I''(u)=-1/(u\ln2)$, so
$g''=\sum_j c_j s_j^{\,2}\,\mathrm I''(u_j)$ equals the stated sum; a concave
function on an interval attains its minimum, and a convex function its maximum,
at an endpoint.
nodes.statement_short: Direct from the identities and $\mathrm I''(u)=-1/(u\ln2)$.

nodes.name: The direction is essential
nodes.statement:
Part \textup{(ii)} bounds $g$ only in the direction its concavity allows: a
\emph{lower} bound from the endpoints requires $g$ concave, an \emph{upper} bound
requires $g$ convex. Endpoint positivity of a \emph{convex} $g$ does not imply
positivity inside; for example $\varepsilon-\mathrm H_2(x)=\varepsilon-\mathrm I(x)
-\mathrm I(1-x)$ is convex and equals $\varepsilon>0$ at $x=0,1$ but
$\varepsilon-1<0$ at $x=\tfrac12$. Accordingly each interval comparison in
Appendices~\ref{sec:affine}--\ref{sec:quarter} first exhibits the sign of $g''$
from the display above and then uses only the matching endpoint bound: the
concave differences give the lower bounds
(Lemmas~\ref{lem:midcomp},~\ref{lem:envdom},~\ref{lem:dom-q}), the convex ones
the upper bounds (the induction of Appendix~\ref{sec:affine} and
Lemma~\ref{lem:B2}). Where the $c_j s_j^{\,2}$ share a sign the sign of $g''$ is
immediate; otherwise it is a rational function, whose sign on $[\alpha,\beta]$ is
checked directly.
nodes.statement_short: Endpoint bounds need the right curvature: concave for lower bounds, convex for upper bounds; example $\varepsilon-\mathrm H_2$.

nodes.name: Certification of (A3)
nodes.statement:
For a point inequality, certificate \textup{(A3)} asserts
$\tfrac13+C-(2-\log_23)=\tfrac73+\log_23-\tfrac53\log_25>0$; by \textup{(i)}, with
$\log_23>\tfrac{19}{12}$ \textup{(}$3^{12}>2^{19}$\textup{)} and
$\log_25<\tfrac73$ \textup{(}$5^{3}<2^{7}$\textup{)},
\[
  \tfrac73+\log_23-\tfrac53\log_25\ >\ \tfrac73+\tfrac{19}{12}-\tfrac53\cdot\tfrac73
  \ =\ \tfrac1{36}\ >\ 0 .
\]

nodes.name: All inequalities are finitely certified
nodes.statement:
Each of the other point inequalities of Lemmas~\ref{lem:exact-q}
and~\ref{lem:cert-q} reduces in the same way to a comparison of integer powers,
the near-degenerate cases using higher convergents of the logarithms; every
reduction is a finite computation. Each interval comparison of
Appendices~\ref{sec:affine}--\ref{sec:quarter} is certified individually by the
second-derivative display in its own proof, which exhibits $\mathrm{sign}\,g''$
on the relevant interval, and its endpoint values are point inequalities of the
same kind.
nodes.statement_short: Every point and interval inequality of the paper reduces to finitely many integer-power comparisons.
